title: Poor service
text:
I have stayed 3 nights at the Kingsbury first week of the October and here is the my view about the place.

Arrival experience was good and front office staff were very friendly and welcoming. They are so attractive and detailed. Even the bell attended who brought my luggage to the room was extremely helpful and he explained everything about the room and services that hotel offered to the guest. 

The breakfast was the most disasters experience I faced there. Service was horrible at the breakfast. Restaurant Hosstess welcome me to the restaurant but she haven’t escorted me to the table and she was expecting me to find my own table I guess. After couple of round at the restaurant I sat down one of the used table and grab a cutlery from next table and had my breakfast, cup of tea or coffee was not offered and I have search couple of times around the buffet that where can I grab a cup of tea. Half a way of my breakfast manager of the restaurant came to me and asked if I wanna have a cup of tea witch I said yes but that cup of tea haven’t arrived till next 30 minutes till I end my breakfast.
Surprisingly Hosstess appear in front of me with the breakfast bill and asked me to sign up. I said my breakfast is included because I have booked a room under the BB . But she is keep saying witch is not included. I have signed the check and walk in to front desk to find out what wrong with the booking. Because I am sure this level of hole should have a strong IT system that internal information can’t be wrong. Somehow FO team confirmed that I am under the BB and after that I have made a complaint about the breakfast service.
Duty manager Amila have offered me a breakfast at the executive lounge witch I appreciate but the service is very poor there as well. 
Second night I went to rooftop lounge and honey beach club during lunch all above areas service is very poor. Staff are gathering and chatting with each other and not focusing on the customers. I have seen from other tables as well almost every table guest needs to raise their hands for the service. Only one good meal I had there was at the Chinese restaurant and service and food was extremely good. 

To recover from breakfast complain Amila has upgraded me to the executive floor room witch I appreciate and Ajith at the front desk was helpful and friendly guy. Hotel needs to look in to F&B service and should improve. 

Generally lovey hotel with clean rooms and offer all the entertainment and facilities for the customers.

title: Average definitely not 5 star
text:
Positives
Hotel itself is very nice with plenty of restaurants and bars
Cons
Whilst the hotel itself is of a good standard the service is not 5 star at all there are staff outside the front of the hotel that don't open the doors for you or greet you when you first get to the hotel nor do they offer to help with your bags.
The food and drinks are overpriced massively you expect them to be higher in a 5 star hotel but not by the amount they are. We did try one of the restaurants and in my pizza I nearly choked on a piece of bone that was in the mince topping they begrudgingly agreed to take that off the bill.
They have a buy one get one free drinks offer for one hour of the day and then try to claim it's not for that drink and you have to order another round to get it free which is not what was agreed and they just smirk and think it's funny.
The concierge service is there just to try flog you massively inflated prices for day trips or hotel cars. Failing that they will try get you into one of their tuk tuks for a tour of Colombo at a rip off price as they get back handers from the tuk tuk drivers.

On the whole the hotel was ok but very average and not 5 star it was at a push 4 star

On a side note for anyone looking at visiting Sri Lanka (this has not reflected my rating on the hotel at all) although this is a beautiful country there isn't much to do in Colombo itself there are just a lot of hotels and not much else. To get to the other places of interest such as Kandy and the Safari parks they are very far away and not able to do within 1 day (Kandy can be done but it is a lot of travelling at least 3 hours each way)
Personally we wouldn't come back to Sri Lanka everyone we met was there to con you trying to take you on tuk tuk tours and charge you massively high rates, fraudsters in the street pretending to be helpful to get you to go to restaurants etc and rip you off and you can't trust anyone to give you honest information. I have never been anywhere like it it seems the whole place works together to try rip you off and their goal is to get as much money as possible out of tourists.

title: Oh dear!!
text:
We visited on our first visit to Sri Lanka several years ago and thought it was a great hotel with great service so when returning to Sri Lanka this year we decided to stay here for our one night in Colombo.  It didn’t start well and went downhill from there.  Check-in wasn’t easy although some of that may have been due to linguistic problems and the noise in the reception area.  The corridor to our rooms in a no smoking area smelt of cigarette smoke though the rooms didn’t.  A suitcase lock was damaged, the restaurant service in the buffet restaurant was at best poor.  The wine we ordered was out of stock, no problem, but when told this we weren’t given the wine list back to chose an alter but had to ask for it. Plates from the table weren’t cleared and we had to move them to another table to ensure we had space for our ongoing meal.  At check-out we had to wait whilst they checked if we’d used the minibar but we couldn’t use it as padlocked.
Highlights were the service in the rooftop bar “Ce la Vi” which was excellent and the chief porter Hussain in resolving our problems with suitcase lock who couldn’t have been more helpful or attentive.  Sadly should we return to Colombo in the future we’ll give the Kingsbury a big miss.

title: Could wait to checkout... What a disappointment
text:
Let me cut to the chase...

Pros:
- Great cup of tea
- Butlers for Suite were very friendly

Cons:
- Service
- Amenities
- Room condition
- Everything you'd expect to be a pro with a hotel when paying $1,000+ per night

I have stayed at all the 5 star, 4 star pretending to be 5 star, new and old, hotels in Colombo. The Kingsbury is hands down the worst experience around!

My wife and I were very much looking forward to spending NYE at The Kingsbury. We'd booked The Kingsbury Suite - their best room.

The Kingsbury has a severe identity crisis! It doesn't know whether it's a Bacardi sponsored, Bali-Esk, pool resort, a W style funky destination or a colonial era, heritage, hotel!?! It's lost!

Now... The suite. It was on the 2nd floor... No view... The staff were still cleaning when we entered... The bathrooms were dirty... The room was dated... The bed was comfortable (only pro about the room).

Apart from the butlers which helped us in the suite, the staff at The Kingsbury are, at best, aloof. They do not show off the best that is Sri Lanka. I pity the traveller who comes here first and thinks that Sri Lanka is like this. As a Sri Lankan myself, I am even more disappointed!

The food is average... The drinks are watered down... It seems to attract a certain "type" of traveller... One who makes a relaxing, romantic, holiday... Impossible! If you are trying to relax and unwind... This is not for you. 

All in all... Stay elsewhere!

title: Worst service
text: One might expect to receive a decent level of service from a 5 star hotel especially after reading all the reviews on TripAdvisor. Unfortunately, I cannot agree. From the time we stepped into the hotel the experience was not great. Our room configuration was incorrect for triple rooms which had to be made up as the rooms were made up with a queen bed only. It didn’t stop there the rooms did not have towels on both days we stayed. The hotel lacks controlling noise, I complained about our neighbors kids playing in the passage and making a racket which went unaddressed for hours. Breakfast layout with food choices was great but the overall service from the waiters were lacking. We repeatedly asked for coffee; tea and water to the point where one of our guest got up to arrange it himself. Tables did not have cutlery either which did not arrive. Poolside service was as bad. On day one I asked for the cocktail menu which didn’t arrive on day 2 we wait 15 minutes before being attended with the menu and again waiters disappeared and we had to go find someone. This continues for the 2 hours we spent at the poolside. There is clearly a lack of customer service all round, I was even advised on calling for room service that the chef was busy.  I eventually complained to our tour operator.  I can’t help but wonder If they were not geared for this busy period.

title: Not up to Scratch
text: that's where it ends with my recent experience. Having spent 8 days in Sri Lanka traveling around and experiencing the best in hospitality i was looking forward to my Kingsbury stay. Upon check in (which might i add was 515pm in the afternoon) i was advised my room was not ready. Something i would accept if before 2pm or close to after. But at over 3 hours past their advertised check in time i questioned this with Reception. After some whispering and keyboard tapping i was told i could have a room. It would be on the executive floor, but was followed up with, no entitlements would be extended, just the room. No problem....we are escorted to the room and bags follow shortly afterwards. The room itself was comfortable with a nice view. However it took 3 phone calls to housekeeping for them to provide adequate towels and toiletries for two guests. Then we tried room service. Two phone calls to place our order. Food did come promptly. I really could write on for days but travellers note...this hotel caters for locals. We were a mother and daughter travelling from Australia and found the majority of staff across the hotel to be rude and condescending. I booked a car through the hotel for the airport. Paid USD65 and told it would be the hotels Mercedes 200E. When we checked out we were loaded into a Volvo i queried this. It was told "Madam they are the same, the door slammed behind me.  Well explain why your hotel car is parked in the driveway! Travellers beware.  Hotel looks great on paper but comes up short.

title: Good in parts
text:
We arrived late afternoon, our room wasn’t ready. Eventually we were allocated a different room; it was OK. We were told we were on a room only basis, which surprised us. We checked this later on our itinerary and indicated this was incorrect; the hotel agreed it should be bed and breakfast. Later on our first night we went for a drink at the roof top bar with friends. I ordered 2 beers and 2 glasses of white wine. I was asked “Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay..” ; I answered Chardonnay, but didn’t check the price. It later turned out that we were being charged R3980 for the 2 glasses, about double the normal rate; you pay R950 per glass in the Kings Bar downstairs. I complained; we hadn’t ordered special wine, so the price looked excessive. We are talking only R2000 in total too much, but it felt as though we were being duped. I thought the front desk handled my complaint poorly, as they had handled our checkin.
Otherwise the hotel is good. The breakfast restaurant and grill food are good, and the pool area if nice, although you do get some exhaust fumes at the road end. 
The hotel is not so close to the sea now; we walked down the road to the Galle Face Hotel and had dinner in the bar close to the sea; a nice evening.
On our last morning we had to leave at 4.15am. I paid my bill the night before; agreed we would pick up a picnic breakfast from the Concierge desk at 4.15am. We actually left at 4.45am (it turned out we had more time) but asking for our picnic breakfast was met with puzzled looks; no breakfast!
Overall the Kingsbury is nice, but I have doubts about the staff at the front desk and the top floor bar.

title: Disappointment -Theft
text: We stayed for 4 days in the executive lounge. The last day we left we left in a hurry to travel to Kandalama to meet our son and future wife. Got to destination phoned Kingsbury reported the missing phone and asked the hotel to search for it as it may have fallen in the room etc. No response was received from hotel. Days later after our trip we came back to hotel to further check and report management. Reported to main police. Now it’s been over a month since we got back to UK nothing received no correspondence from Kingsbury. We left our details no reply. They said investigation will be made. We knew we will never get it back. But .  We are sure it was taken from room. While the hotel boasts luxury the level of communication to retain good paying customers is very poor on this occasion . After spending £1000 for 4 days the level of customer service is very poor. Guys be aware to keep your things locked in safe at all times as sticky fingers are about in this hotel -  got a new phone from office now  but the whole experience Very Disappointing.

The Breakfast buffet offers a wonderful spread including lots of Sri Lankan specialties. 

On the downside, the land around the hotel is now part of a huge reclamation project. 24/7 you can see earth movers doing their thing. No view of the sea. The pool must have been on the edge of the sea at one time, but now just borders a small road with traffic. Very weird! The rooftop bar has the same fate. At some time it must have given a beautiful view over the sea, now it just overlooks unending sand!

Bottom line: stay if you’re a business traveler with little time for leisure at the hotel. Otherwise choose another property in Colombo.

title: Adequate stay for a night or two
text: We stayed at The Kingsbury on our first two nights in Sri Lanka before heading off to explore the rest of the country. We also stayed there on our final night before heading back to the airport (the night linked to this review) and, to be honest, if our hotel room hadn't been non-refundable, we probably wouldn't have stayed a second time. That's not to say the hotel isn't fine, it's just not for us. It's got quite a lively feel to the place, which will be great for many, especially the Honey Pool Bar. But, for those wanting to rest before or after a long plane journey, it doesn't offer the calmest pitstop. This is particularly the case because the Honey Pool Bar plays loud music until fairly late whether people are outside or not, which can be heard in all poolside facing bedrooms.  The rooms themselves are clean and functional (though on our first trip there were a few large hairs hanging off the hairdryer etc) and there's a nice selection of toiletries for travellers. The TV remote didn't work particularly well in either room.  We ordered room service on our first night, which arrived very late and quite a while after the accompanying drinks. However, we also ate two delicious meals at the Ocean Seafood restaurant and the Grill (attached to Harbour Court). For those newly arrived in Sri Lanka, make sure you have a few tip-size notes ready. The hotel already serves a 10% service charge but we felt very awkward when tips were clearly expected for our room service though we didn't have any cash ready yet and the room service hadn't been great.   The hotel is very well located nr to Galle Face and opposite the Dutch Hospital. For that reason, I think what looks like airbrushing of the location on the photos is a bit unnecessary. Colombo is a bustling city going through fast change and so we obviously didn't mind seeing constructions works, roads skyscrapers etc but the photos for the Kingsbury would have you believe the swimming pool is almost on the beach itself not next to a car park separated by a main road, albeit looking out on a stretch of sand, and that the hotel is set back in gardens. The hotel and the location is fine, just don't be disappointed by the difference!

title: Looks the part - menu and service not good
text:
Whilst spending a week in Sri Lanka I visited The Kingsbury. It’s a 5 Star hotel but a little bit trendy and a great Grill Restaurant. I have visited the Grill before and it’s very good. 

This time I had two Indian colleagues with me who were vegetarian so we opted to sit in the Bar area, have a drink and watch the IPL on TV. 

 We looked at the menu and there was no vegetarian option.  I could not order from The Grill ( fair enough) so my colleagues only option was the Room Service menu. 

The option was Cheeseboard ( plastic cheese and Jacobs crackers) and a veg platter which consisted of a potato cut in slices , an onion cut in slices and some pepper cut in slices. 

I won’t mention the Hotel I was staying in but the offer there has a whole vegetarian buffet section and the chef came across personally to my colleagues to advise if they wanted anything made to let him know. 

Now I am not vegetarian but am in the hotel and food business and know how cheap it is to make quality vegetarian food. Are you honestly telling me that a 5 Star hotel in this day and age has a veg option of crackers and cheese and sliced vegetables. 

Kitchen department - shame on you and if I was Exec chef I would be looking to find any valid reason at the moment! 

The pic attached is the other hotel where we stayed. This was the vegetarian offer there. 

Even though I am an avid carnivore I am astonished that this is acceptable in 2018 

God help them if they ever get a Vegan staying !

title: Worse customer service at the pool side bar - 05/05/2018
text:
I've visited on 05/05/18. This review is for the Kingsbury pool side bar. We were a group of three, decided to grab something to eat and drink by the pool side bar after enjoying the acoustic tunes at the kings lounges.

Once our order got served, heavy rains collapsed, leaving us no time to move to somewhere. The table umbrella was useless; had holes and the water poured onto our foods and drinks and leaving us soaking wet. We waved at a number of poolside servers passing by our table, no one reacted and totally ignored us. I don't know what happened to the person should have looked after our table, I managed to get attention one of the server after 20 - 25 minutes, he managed to take out two of my friends inside, and decided himself to put the bill; leaving me in rain further (fr'king unbelievable). 
There was no way, I was going to leave the place without speaking to the manager. Made a booking on Hotels.com and arrived at hotel at 13 hours, doormen bell boys did there job perfectly and moved to reception desk and showed them my booking on phone. Asked me so many questions about the booking and asked me to wait for 2 minutes while they get my documents ready for check in. Kids were tired so we sat on a sofa at the lobby. 15 minutes past and no one came to us, not a glass of water even.
I saw many foreign and local guest relations officers walking and talking to each other but not attending guests matters. Went back to the desk and asked about my booking, and then they replied " sorry, our system is down. Just give us 2 minutes"
I replied, ok...then I'll go to the bar have something, come to me when room is ready.
Spend 1 hour 15 minutes at the bar, not a single massage from the desk.
As we were getting to the peak of our patience I ask the barman to call and ask my room is ready or not. 
He personal ly went few steps to the reception desk and came back with a answer askng us to wait another 2 minutes.
Fine, we waited another 5 to 10 minutes. 
Then I thought of speaking to a gro explained what happened, she walked to the reception desk with me and asked them to check on my reservation and got wanished through a door close by.
What poor guest relations work is this, got mad.
Raised the voice a bit and two seconds my room was given...but not the type of room I booked, they said the port city has bloked the sea view, but it is not.... it's there own building!
Came and appologized, room was upgraded to a smoke filled room, a fruit basket was sent to room ....BUT
Things would have easier, friendlier and more hospitable if people around  took there job seriously and attend in to. There slogan "forever timeless" they have taken it wrong,

title: Hit and miss really
text:
So stayed here for a total of 2 nights at the end of 2 weeks in sri lanka .
Check in was smooth , i arrived early so had to wait by pool for room to be ready , even though they told me they would let me know i had to go back to reception and check again .
Room was nice , all you need really .
I decided to have food at 14:30 , this was a little confusing with so many options and one buffet closing another just opening and not much clarity on what was open .
Opted for a burger by pool .
No Corona for the two days i stayed at the pool bar yet they had it at night on terrace bar , surely a 5 star hotel should sort these minor details out ?
Had a massage whilst here that was very uncomfortable and borderline sleazy .
A lot if suited “managers” around just floating !
Attempted to arrange a taxi to airport and was quoted 10,000 at front desk ! Walked outside and booked a local one for 3,000 , shame really not everyone wants a limo !
Pool was nice but was spoilt by the building site opposite , truck after truck all day long ! 
Although the stay was above average i wouldn’t consider this a 5* anymore with the likes of cinnamon and shangreela near by . 
So to summarise if you get a bargain they stay here , if you are after the full package maybe not .

title: Fair Enough For A Night - Nothing Exceptional
text:
The Kingsbury is OK.  The management, like so many on the waterfront, must be totally annoyed by the landfill work going on ensuring that the view is marred by a vast building site. Not much they can do about that.

What the management can do is get their act together on other areas.

Check in took a lifetime.  They don't manage the queue, much jumping and pushing in, not enough people behind the desk and when they do finally check you in, it takes forever; so much faffing about.  Fortunately, we were only off a short flight, but if you had just come long haul...

The room itself is not large.  It also feels a bit worn.  Bathroom is OK and the windows large (onto that view) but the rest? Not much.  Very ordinary, even with all the fiddly bits.  There are clear attempts to be "more" (chocolates etc.) but unless you deliver a true experience, forget it.  Just take your price down a bit.  

Door staff were not willing to pull in tuk-tuks.  The thing is, tuk-tuks use meters in Columbo, starting at 50R.  That is great.  But by not pulling them in, guests are subject to the two - three rip off drivers just outside the hotel. They are trying to charge 5 - 10 times the going rate for a trip ("Meter broken", all that jazz).  Don't fall for it, but something says there is a door staff / driver mafia going on with kick backs to the door staff.  Who wants to stay in a hotel where management are not in control of that?

Adding to this, on departure, this left us needing to haul our luggage out to the street (with a three year old in tow) having requested a taxi.  "Tuk-tuk?" replied the lazy doorman.  No, but he pointed that way, then watched us. Cheers.

The pool is decent - and the one standout performance goes to the pool area manager.  Engaging, helpful and keeping a watchful eye out for kids.  Perhaps appoint him as GM?  He'd have a better view of guest care.  Food and beverage service at the pool is sloooooow.  Trying to get attention.  We assume the loud music in the afternoon was for Christmas Eve.  If not, and they do call it the "Honey Beach Club", then I would suggest to avoid the entire hotel if you are after a relaxing pool experience,  Thump, thump, thump. And the music / DJ was not even good which might have helped. 

Breakfast was fine - if you helped yourself to everything: cutlery, serviettes etc.  Don't seek staff help.  See the theme here?

In terms of location, it is well positioned within the Fort area and close to the Dutch Hospital (5 minutes walk, maximum).  But that can be said about a few other hotels within spitting distance.  So not really a selling point.

All very disappointing, after the very pleasant arrival experience at the airport and the courteous hotel driver.  There's a thought - make him and the pool guy the senior managers.

The lobby is full of guests going in and out and it’s like a busy transit lounge. The poolside and the Grill is far too hot. The roof top is closed during the day and there isn’t anywhere to have a relaxing drink. The Gourmet Station which is the snack counter of the hotel is dysfunctional most of the time because it is turned into a high tea buffet for most of the afternoon.

The Kings pub is a dark lifeless place. The Chinese restaurant is full of frills but the taste and the portion sizes fail to impress. The Buffets in the harbour Court are very good value for money and quite extensive. There is a lot of repetition though of the same item in different colours. 

Wine by the bottle is around Rs 1,000/- to 2,000/ higher than at similar hotels. Spirits too are quite expensive. Buy your own wine and spirits at a super market (before 9 pm and when it’s not a holiday for the full moon) and have it in your room where there is some peace and quiet.

title: If you want authentic “High Tea” in Colombo, Sri Lanka, avoid the one at the Kingsbury Hotel.
text:
There are several places one could opt to have “High Tea” in Colombo, Sri Lanka. If you are the type that enjoys a quiet afternoon authentic “High Tea” in Colombo, Sri Lanka,  the place to visit is certainly not Kingsbury Hotel.  This hotel has a lot of pluses such as its location but it has not learnt the art of presenting an authentic “High Tea”, even allowing for some variations to please the local palate. One would have to look for some other place in Colombo that does a better job or go to London to experience the mystique English afternoon High Tea at one of the famous departmental stores in Central London or better still wait for an invitation by Queen Elizabeth to have tea with her!

The tradition of afternoon High Tea originated in England during the early 19th century. At that time, it is claimed that people of England had only two meals – breakfast and dinner around 8 pm. This made some people weary and out of sorts by late afternoon. Anna, the Seventh Duchess of Bedford was one such person and she got into the habit of drinking tea accompanied by some finger food such as dainty sandwiches and sweet pastries, to get over the late afternoon blues. At first, she went through this ritual alone in her room. Later, she invited her friends to join her and eventually, it became a living room event, with more participants and a greater variety of sandwiches and pastries. This event soon spread to all regions of the United Kingdom and the colonies and eventually all over the world via five - star hotels and specialty restaurants. Variations of the traditional High Tea also popped up in several countries. The traditional English High Tea was modified in many countries by the introduction of local meat/fish based spicy savories to suit local palates. This is especially so in the Asian countries where the local spicy goodies are more popular than scones, cucumber sandwiches and sweet pastries.

I was recently in Doha, Qatar where I had “High Tea” at the West End Café at Marriott Hotel situated in Doha Bay. It was similar to the original British version than the somewhat modified High Teas served in many countries. It follows the British tradition of serving buttermilk and raisin scones with fresh strawberry jam and clotted cream, followed by a variety of sandwiches – Cucumber, Pickle, Crème Fraiche, Chives, Smoked Turkey Ham, Plum Chutney, Smoked Salmon, Roe, Egg, Cherry Tomato, Mozzarella and Basil. The pastry offerings included Strawberry, Macaroon, Cream Éclair, White Chocolate and Cream Cheese. Desserts included Chocolate Fondue, Skewers of Marshmallows, Pineapple and Strawberry Chocolate Brownies. There was a wide selection of loose tea or coffee.

Each order was made fresh. The offerings were not made buffet style as in most five-star hotels in Sri Lanka including Kingsbury Hotel.  This ensured freshness. The ambience was just perfect for enjoying a quiet afternoon, imbibing tea and the goodies at one’s own pace.

I was looking for not exactly the same experience but something close to it at the Kingsbury Hotel. But I was in for a rude shock. I would not describe the offering at Kingsbury Hotel as anything close to a typical “High Tea”. It was a huge crowded buffet with all kinds of snacks, salads, cakes and savories. Even chicken wings and all kinds of pickles were part of the offering. At one stage, I was looking for the “tea” which escaped my eyes. I asked some waitstaff where I could find some “tea”. All that they did was to point me in a certain direction. They did not have the courtesy to “guide” me to the exact location. Finally when I got to the “tea station”, I asked for a pot of tea. Instead, I was pointed to an urn of hot water. I asked for tea and was pointed to a series of tea bags, most prominent of which was green tea. I asked for cream.  I was pointed to a small container that was kept on the urn of hot water. At that point, I just gave up in great disappointment and desperation and returned home. I did not want to even go back to my table as it was not easy to navigate through all the small tables with four chairs, placed in close proximity to each other. Every time I left my table, some other “High Tea patrons” would occupy my chair and I had to look for another table. I had to change my table three times. The atmosphere was worse than a crowded bus or railway station in Colombo.

I have not been to most of the other places that serve “High Tea” in Colombo except for the Hilton Hotel and Cinnamon Grand Hotel. At both these places, my experience was much more satisfying. 

My verdict: If you want to experience “High Tea” in Colombo, Sri Lanka, you will do well to avoid the one at Kingsbury Hotel.

title: Found a DEAD COCKROACH in my drink at GRILL Restaurant . Beware of what you drink and eat !
text:
This incident occurred on 27th August 2017 at The Grill Restaurant around 2.30 pm .I was out there having a late lunch with a friend and this whole situation ruined the moment and what is more disheartening is to see how light the management of Kingsbury  took this matter  and went on ignoring  .  I think it is my duty to let the public aware, so that they can be sure next time before they eat and drink .  
To my absolute disgust, there was a DEAD COCKROACH in my Passion Mojito (which had clearly been deceased for some time, it may have already held its funeral by that stage! RIP!!)  I was shell shocked to see the DEAD COCKROACH  and was sick to my stomach after seeing this. This is not incidental, a cockroach cannot just creep in, there has to be an infestation or their preparation areas are not up to the accepted hygiene standards otherwise you wouldn’t find a cockroach in your drink. We cannot merely  excuse after discovering a DEAD COCKROACH in your drink served at an establishment like Kingsbury. That is a severe hygiene matter and I am surprised how weakly and rudely the management of this hotel responded to this issue. 
I went on to point out the  severity of such a discovery and I brought this matter to the attention of the GM’s Office , Customer Manager  Shenara and Dilshan the F&B Manager  yet eventually none provided a positive feedback .
It’s been almost a month when  I received a letter from General Manager without mentioning a single apology , he went on stating “Alleged that your drink was contaminated” .It was well proven that there was a DEAD COCKROACH in the drink and the time of the incident there were responsible staffers including Dilshan the F&B Assistant Manager, Supervisor and the Bar Manager who obviously noticed what was going on and they knew and acknowledged that is their issue took the cockroach and the drink off the table. Apparently  the  Manager  further stated that “ Several Telephone Conversations I have had and demanded further compensation “  . Again he was referring to an  incident  had happened during a  Dinner ,  may be he was referring to another Cockroach incident took place and sent me the wrong letter I suppose. It was obviously a lunch and I am sure the higher Management  was not well informed on the whole incident with facts .
However, they waived off the bill even though I did not continue to eat the food we ordered , they offered coffee and a scoop of ice cream at my reluctance and I can see the GM mentioned  in his letter that the staff  offered free coffee and Ice Cream like they offered the best to compensate us . We left the place and hopped in to another hotel to have  our lunch. On 24th SEP  I was offered a 4 pax dinner on complimentary which I graciously DECLINED because I was not looking for free dinners which does not suit my capacity .I don’t think free dinners can fix such a sever issue of this capacity at a five star hotel . 
I have contacted the team at Kingsbury and unfortunately they shaved their ears for my concerns and went on neglecting. My concern is, the Senior Management  did not take this matter seriously to pay the right attention and did not even extend a proper apology to us .Very unacceptable !
I have been patronizing their facilities such as meeting rooms, restaurants,accommodation etc before and even sent our foreign delegates we are working with  and it will not be the same in the future anyways .In the past , there were certain situations where the service and the quality was not that great , yet I was fine  and gave it a miss because none was critical like  this yet I gave positive feedback  . 
I would like to bring this to the attention of those who dine in this hotel , beware of what you eat and drink , you never know you would accidentally eat a full grown cockroach !

text:

The variety of food was very poor and cheap. The taste was not at all great. It was not horrible but not good roo. There were very basic food and it was quite cheap and mostly only veg food. The salads were only veg.  There was a sandwich named "beef" but when i ate it, it was "salmon". The platter with "chicken burgers" and "french fries" were empty every time i went to take them. I am not at all happy with it, it felt really cheap and useless.There's better variety and quality in near by hotels for less money too.

title: The noise ruins this hotel - avoid
text: This hotel is impressive when you arrive however I have stayed in hostels that have been much quieter and whose staff actually responded to noise complaints. I requested a quiet room on arrival as I had a long haul flight the next day that I needed to be awake at 5:30am for. I was assured I would be given a quiet room however I was directly opposite the outdoor pool/nightclub area. When I asked to be moved to a quieter room, without looking on the computer I was told by the front desk that they are completely booked and then stared at until I left without an alternative. I was also told that it stops at 11pm, this is untrue. I must assume the man at the front desk lied to me because at 11:20pm when it continued as loud as ever, I was told it stops at 12am. This is not acceptable for a hotel claiming to be 5 star. I wouldn't accept this from a hostel. Two other details - one of the complimentary bottles of water in my room had already been opened (I told the front desk - again without an apology or explanation I was simply given another) and there were red stains on the sheets that looked very much like blood. Very unimpressed with this hotel and I will not be staying again when I return - book elsewhere, there are plenty of cheaper alternatives that I'm sure will be better than this place.

We were on the 4th floor and had the view of Galle Face road. Except that we can also see the cemented platform above the reception area from our window that needs some simple landscaping. 

We have had much more refined stays at luxury hotels in different parts of the world and would not recommend checking in here if there is a choice.

That said, I was leading a group of 21 friends (using 11 rooms) on a visit to Sri Lanka -- we stayed at The Kingsbury our first night and then, a week later, on our last night. Our tour operator and our local guide made it abundantly clear that our group was NOT to be charged for non-alcoholic drinks that came with dinner but there apparently was NO communication between the front desk and the restaurant leading to a very annoying and embarrassing situation for me. Ultimately, the restaurant supervisor insisted I accompany him to the front desk where they did not want to do anything to correct this but when I told them that unless it was fixed then and there I would let other travelers know of their incompetence via Trip Advisor. The next morning it was addressed successfully but not one word of apology! This is no way to run a hotel.

title: Very comfortable beds, haphazard service
text:
The beds in this hotel are AMAZING! I would stay in this hotel again for this reason alone - it was like waking up in a cloud! There was also a lovely rainforest shower and jacuzzi bath in our room - much welcomed. The pool is also nice and well kept.
Apart from that...I think it is overpriced for what the hotel is and I'm pretty sure it's not a 5 star hotel by world standards. The service was clumsy - poolside tea served without milk and by the time they brought the milk the tea was cold. Chocolate 'lava' cake served stone cold with melted ice cream. A steak restaurant that didn't give you the wine and food menu at the same time, didn't serve red wine in red wine glasses, deserts were served at different times even though we asked if they could come together. The breakfast was fine but not a particularly wide variety. Pretty amusing paintwork in the rooms, dodgy light fittings and a housekeeping 'manager' that basically walked into our room directly after knocking to check everything was fine...it would have been if we hadn't been changing into our swimwear at the time ;-) 
It's a real shame that there is construction work going on right beside the hotel so the infinity pool view is now pretty sad. Not the hotel's fault but should they really be charming the same rates when you are sunbathing whilst listening to construction work and offering views of excavators from your bedroom window?

title: Mixed Feelings
text:
This hotel looks 5 star, has the amenities of a 5 star hotel and staff are trained as such. However, when we checked in there was a huge crowd at the lobby and there was lots of people out and about, something I rarely see at 5-star establishments. There was a queue at check in and one of our rooms was not available then so we went out and came back at night, only to find out it was given away but they were gracious enough to offer us an upgrade and discounted rates on extended stay due to our flight timings. I have to thank the guy at the lobby (sorry, his name slipped my mind) for helping us business travelers with this.

The lobby itself is always seemingly populated with people, events and music which can be a little unexpected though I was generally fine with that. It is a drastic difference, however, when you walk to Hilton etc. 

The interior room decor speaks for itself. You feel like you're living in a grand room with a nice personalized welcome message on your screen. Products were Bvlgari etc and it was a nice touch to the entire experience. Rooms overlooked the beach but sadly there's reclamation and construction going on so it was a little weird when I saw how the pool looked out to a road and construction area from my hotel room. 

My room was a standard room and I could hear what the couple staying next door were saying and plastic bag noises when they were packing through the wooden connecting door. Thankfully they did not stay up through the night. You can also hear kids or guests speaking in the corridor however it is generally fine if your neighbors are respectful at appropriate times of the day. 

Location is fine, we generally used the app to call for transport as bargaining at the roadside was often a rip off and time consuming. 

Overall, it is a nicely decorated place but a little different experience from what I would expect at a 5 star establishment and I'm not if it's worth the cost.

title: Noisy location
text:
A word of caution before booking this hotel.  I last stayed here 10 years ago, when it was known as the Ceylon Continental.  However, the hotel has been completely revamped in recent years and was renamed The Kingsbury.  Sadly for them they seemingly didn’t include soundproofing of the rooms as part of this process.

I booked on the executive floor for 3 nights on the run up to Christmas.  The room, although small compared to other hotels of its class, was well appointed and practical with a king size bed with views of the trade tower, promenade and Galle Face Green - or what’s left of it!  All you see now are three humongous hotels now being constructed along the prom, which has completely ruined the landscape the way it was a few years ago.  Bulgari toiletries were supplied and there was a decent walk-in shower.  

The executive lounge was tiny compared to other hotels I’ve stayed at.  It was plain and sterile and took on the look of a café with tables and chairs.  No sofas or easy chairs to relax on.  Although the staff were friendly and attentive, it was a huge disappointment.   I didn’t see any dedicated exec floor check in either.  

I was offered an upgrade from the hotel to the executive floor, which I accepted for an additional $20 a night.  I know realise why the offer came through as evidence suggests they were far from full on the executive floor.  I later found out why.

Issues occurred during the evening when I retired for the day.  There was set of earplugs in the bedside draw and I thought to myself why on earth they would do that?  I’ve never seen that in any other hotel I’ve stayed at.  The reason soon became clear.  I didn’t get a wink of sleep because of a music festival on one side of the hotel, which continued until 3am, and 24-hour construction on the other side.  Clearly the rooms are not soundproofed.  The noise was truly horrendous and the earplugs made no difference.  Although they tried their best and moved me to another room on the other side of the hotel facing the harbour, the 24-hour construction didn’t change anything.  I’m talking mechanical diggers and lorries coming and going all night.  When I passed this by the duty manager he said there was nothing they could do about the construction of “Fun City” and the music festival was on for the remainder of the week.

This prompted me to cut my three night stay and check out the very next morning and I did exactly that and moved to the exec floor of the Cinnamon Grand hotel, which I have stayed at for many years.  The Kingsbury management were professional and helpful, but there was clearly little they could do to resolve the noise situation or guest’s comfort.  

I was impressed with the hotel revamp on comparing it to the way it looked 10 years ago.  If they had soundproofed the rooms, then that would have helped.  I found breakfast buffet to be chaotic in many ways.  The idea that they cook the likes of sausages and bacon from raw in front of you while you wait is fine, but sadly results in huge queues.  Because I was delayed at the buffet, my assigned table was taken upon my return to it, meaning I had to look for another table, food in hand, as they were packed at the time.  The buffet is huge and plentiful for all tastes, but on reflection I think it’s too big.  The concept is nice, but isn’t practical in my opinion.  I think the biggest disappointment was the ongoing construction.  Who wants to sit at the pool and look at that?   Same goes for the night pool bar with the constant drone of construction in the background.  

The hotel is centrally located for the city and everything is within reasonable walking distance.  This is one reason why I chose to return, but then sadly events then took over.  I doubt if I will ever stay here again.  It looks to me as if the construction will take several years to complete.   I think it’s only fair to warn potential travellers.

title: Satisfactory hotel, centrally located
text: We spent two nights at the Kingsbury. The hotel itself has a unique colonial feel and charm to it.  The ocean views are a bit marred due to the ongoing large-scale port construction, so that was a little disappointing.  The wifi is spotty and the hotel is often hosting many events (weddings + conferences) so there are usually crowds in the lobby during the morning and evening hours.  The on-site restaurants are very good, and the breakfast buffet was very impressive with a large variety of Sri Lankan and English breakfast options.  I really enjoyed the ambience of the rooftop bar for an evening cocktail and snack as well.  I used the gym facilities which were modern and spacious, but because it was located on the street-level and has large windows, people walking by would stare inside, which was uncomfortable for me as a young female working out alone in the gym.  I am unsure as to whether I would return to stay at the hotel again or try a different hotel in Colombo next time.

title: Would not recommend
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 3 days.  On check in, the hotel put a hold on our credit card to cover the booking, which is normal procedure and at that point was no problem (I will come back to this).  

The good - The hotel is in a great location and close to the Dutch Hospital shopping/restaurants (practically across the road), and easy to get a tuk-tuk into the city and around.  It is not too far from the Pettah Markets but would suggest a tuk-tuk. Easy walk to Galle Face Green.

The not good - on two occasions (that we know of) our room door would not lock.  Something wrong with the electronic locking system and maintenance had to fix it.  The lifts don't have security access, so anyone off the street can access the hotel floors.  Rooms are OK but for the price, there are better hotels in Colombo.  

3 days after checking out, I checked my credit card and found that whilst I had paid my account in full, the money held on check in had not been released.  I emailed the Hotel and they advised it was my banks fault.  I contacted my bank and they had not received the authorisation from the hotel to release my funds and they needed that first.  After 3 weeks of emailing the General Manager of the hotel, Mr Scott Mawhinney (who never once replied), contacting the Global Payment company, and numerous international phone calls to my bank, I managed to get the funds released after I had arrived home.  To date, I have not received an apology from the hotel.  I also know that this happened to another guest (as the hotel shared with me), so clearly their process is faulty.

title: Highs and Lows Aplenty
text: It is with a heavy heart that I review the Kingsbury as it is a hotel of extreme contrasts and wherever I go I try to be objective and fair-minded when it comes to reviewing places, people and experiences anywhere in the world. A colleague and I stayed for 7 days while we were presenting at and attending an international conference at the BMICH. The highs are the food. There is a wide variety of choice, and it was all of high quality, and the people front and back of house are thoroughly professional in food service. Rooms were large, very clean and oh the beds and pillows! They were so comfortable; I'd never been so comfortable in any hotel bed. Laundry service is efficient and they do an outstanding job in cleaning and protecting valuable business attire. The guards I used to chat with early in the morning especially near the pool area were charming and such delightful men to talk with. They were the public face of the hotel as far as I was concerned and they were wonderful people. I should also praise the people who helped us with IT support in the business centre who made sure our technical glitches and problems were solved fast. Now for the bad parts. The wifi in this hotel is unsatisfactory. It is so slow I couldn't even back up an Iphone! Irrespective of whether you use the room or public wifi it is simply not serviceable. This is also a noisy hotel. There were many functions in the evening and the music and yelling could be heard across floors late into the evening. I had to go to bed with noise cancelling headphones on 3 nights to blot it out. There was also the matter of the hotel travel bureau/desk. On a day off we agreed to pay a fixed and final fee for a car and driver for a day's travel to an elephant sanctuary and Kandy. We set off early in a Kia wagon with Kingsbury livery and by the time we'd left Colombo it was apparent we were being touted. We did see the elephants and this was a wonderful experience. However, instead of the time we wished to spend in Kandy, the driver closed out the maximum available time in a day trip by attempting to tout us for the duration of the day. First was a spice farm where we could make donations and buy products, then it was a tea factory with the same modus operandi. We'd been on the road since 6.45 am and this guy continued to attempt to talk us into stopping at a gemstone store and a temple before we had lunch in Kandy at almost 2 pm and then afterward he continued to insist we stop at various furniture, gem, and clothing stores on the return trip. When we advised him we were not interested in visiting these places he continued his patter trying to break us down presumably. I had to put it to him assertively that we wanted to return to the hotel immediately with no further unwanted diversions. He then became sulky. On return to the hotel he wanted to be paid in cash and I refused as the deal with the hotel travel bureau was that it would be added to the hotel bill. Inside, the travel desk presented me with a voucher on which they wanted me to write my room number, name and my signature to a form with no details! I refused until they completed the form. They then raised the agreed price from 16000 to 21000 in the local currency! I refused and insisted they adhere to the original cost agreement as the driver had already been tipped by my colleague in cash. They scratched out the 21000 and replaced it with16000 and I signed the voucher. When I checked out, the amount billed on the final hotel bill had been upped to 21000 and not the 16000 I had signed for. This is called fraud in my country. I understand the touting game and appreciate why it happens. What I will not brook is a driver contracted by a hotel touting us and ruining our only full day off work, and the alteration of a signed document for a service. We will return to Sri Lanka and Colombo, but will not stay at this hotel again. I am pursuing this through Booking.com who processed the reservation.

title: Service needs major improvement
text:
Pros: The lobby is tastefully decorated and often filled with visiting dignitaries and wedding parties. The Senses Spa is also quite well done and indeed a pleasure to visit; various 90 minute massages were, with an ‘early bird’ 20% discount about $90. The rooms have an abundance of hot water, the king sized bed was comfortable and it was very quiet.  As the whole floor was “smoke free” there were no tobacco odors in the hall or rooms. The morning buffet was extensive and all the food seemed fresh and was tasty.

Cons: Unfortunately the cons do out weigh the pros. The hall carpets need to be thoroughly cleaned or replaced and the room needed to be repainted and the air conditioning frame was broken as was the plastic shield at the base of the shower door. I also detected some mold in the bath room. One only gets a full ocean view if you take the suite at a not so sweet $450 a nite.

Service was terrible. Starting with the buffet, most of the time the tables were set without napkins and you’d have to ask for one. Coffee, if requested, came late or not at all. In the room we would request wash clothes and often it would take several requests and sometimes hours later they would appear and would not be replaced unless once again requested.  Often the bath mat was not replaced and spare toilet paper was not left unless requested, and then not replaced unless once again requested. Oh yes, the spa: though we had made reservations for the two of us the day before they had forgotten to write them down. As a result we had to return 1 ½ hours later when they had some masseuses available. Typical. And when the WiFi went out around 6 PM I had to wait until 8 AM the next morning when the “IT” person came in; yes, they couldn’t have called him in to make sure that a whole hotel’s guests had WiFi?

As newer hotels with ocean views come on line, I can see customers avoiding the Kingsbury if possible.

title: Dishonest practice at the Grill
text:
Firstly, I must emphasize that we did not stay at the hotel. We just visited its restaurant The Grill as we wanted some nice steak. We were approached by a waiter with its wine menu. He informed us that all the bottles on the wine menu was at half price. We took a look at the menu and picked a bottle which we like. It was priced at about S$ 80. After factoring the 50% discount, we thought S$40 is a very reasonable price for a bottle. 

We then ordered two steak medium rare. My steak turned out to be almost well done, which was very disappointing.

But the biggest disappointment was at the presentation of the final bill. We noticed the restaurant charged us S$80 for the bottle of wine. We enquired about the bill with the same waiter about the 50% discount which he had earlier informed us. To our dismay, he said that the price that was reflected in the menu was AFTER discount!!

In our view, this is the MOST dishonest practice I have ever come across! If you present a wine menu to a customer and tell the customer that all the bottles are at 50% off, naturally, the customer will think the menu prices are BEFORE discount. There was nothing written on the menu that the prices are AFTER discount. 

We were obviously very displeased with the restaurant but did not want to kick up a big fuss. So we just paid for our meal and left. 

However, I will advise guests and tourists NEVER to patronise the Grill. And if u should, caveat emptor- buyers beware! But honestly, i think it shouldnt be like that. Tourists should feel safe and not constantly worry about whether they are going to be fleeched.

title: 5 Star Ambience with 2 Star Service
text:
This is a beautiful hotel. If beautiful with an Art Deco feel is what you want, then this is your hotel. If you want responsive staff that see to your needs...then pick another hotel.

1. We arrived with 4 large suitcases. When asking for a bellhop (bag courier) I was directed to go to another desk. The gentleman at the desk was not busy and could have easily summoned a bell hop or called the other desk to summon a bell hop. I wasn't about to spend time running from desk to desk trying to get one of the three idle bell hops to assist. Meanwhile my husband hauled our luggage out of the cab while 3 bell hops watched. Not one offered help. When I went to try to get a luggage cart myself then and only then did a bell hop suddenly appear. 

2. The phone in our room was broken. My husband called down stairs for someone to fix it. The reception balked at sending someone up to fix the issue, because he could just use the phone in the hall by the elevators. They eventually sent someone up to replace the phone. The gentlemen then seemed to linger for a tip. 

3. We requested a bellhop for the following morning at 9 a.m. At 9:10 we called to find out if someone was coming. They had forgotten we wanted assistance with our bags. 

4. We checked out. Not one departing greeting was offered. 

5. Construction surrounds the hotel on both sides. Unless you are able to get a room with an ocean view - it may not be too picturesque. 

We've stayed in a few hotels and B&Bs in Sri Lanka, the Kingsbury is either making a killing with their bookings and their ability to care has completely gone out the window or there is extremely poor management. 

I would not recommend this hotel.

title: Great staff
text:
This is an old property that has been upgraded. 

Our room and bed were comfortable and the staff tried hard but unfortunately the hotel doesn't really cut it.

We started out on the 9th (executive floor) but the noise from the function area above meant no sleep. The hotel moved us to a similar room on level 3, but unfortunately it didn't enjoy the same level of maintenance. (Paint and carpet were in need of attention and the Air-conditioning control didn't always seem to work.) 

Getting fresh towels after room servicing depended on whether the 'washing' had been done that day. Clearly they have insufficient stock.

The staff in the executive lounge were outstanding. Nothing was too much trouble. We had breakfast there each day and the selection and freshly cooked eggs were good. Drinks and canapés in the evening were acceptable but not especially remarkable. Unfortunately they oversell the facility so on some nights we were unable to get a table.

The buffet in the main restaurant was very good, and again the staff was great. 

Unfortunately connecting to the Internet was a minute-to-minute proposition with regular dropouts and poor service on the 3rd floor. Eventually the executive lounge supplied me with a different modem that worked well. We also had 2 (fairly short) power outages during our stay.

The hotel attracts numerous functions, many of which are held on the 10th floor and the rooftop bar above. The two elevators simply do not cope. Often they are full and sometimes you have a long wait. This becomes extremely frustrating if you are rushing to a business appointment or conference session.

In summary, great staff but management shortcomings devalue the hotel.

title: Cubbyholish - would not reccomend!
text:
I stayed for one night and was sorely disappointed! 
The lobby is like a railway station, as is frequented by many locals and non hotel guests. Infact the lobby level outlets like the Kings Bar etc have mostly non hotel guests and it feels crowded, noisy and disorienting to be there.
For a 150 dollars what you get is way below the mark, say compared to any other hotel for 25 to 50 dollars more!!
I was apparently upgraded from a superior to a premium room, so shudder to think how small the superior would be.
Rooms apparently renovated only 3 years ago, but doesn't seem that way, maybe overused hotel!
There is no real view as is apparent from my picture, as it overlooks the roof of the lobby and sea in distance.
My room was on the 3rd floor, fairly small, ok bathroom, no bathtub.
However the shower was good. 
The bed was a large King, could easily fit 2 adults and a older kid, and was very comfortable, the biggest positive for the hotel if you ask me!
Service was not too bad, they did give me late check out for few hours.
Spa seemed v overpriced, I didn't try it.
Housekeeping could definitely do a better job! See attached picture of table in my room.
Breakfast was normal like most 5 stars, nothing out of the ordinary. 
Swimming pool really sucked as was adjacent to the parking lot, with the infinity part overlooking the public road! Definitely a lack of privacy and not a great ambience for a pool. No wonder I never saw anyone using the pool!
All in all I feel there are a zillion better options in Colombo for a similar price, or a little more so why would anyone opt for this? Yes, if it was a 100 dollar hotel then acceptable, which is what it should be in my view!
I got swayed by the reviews on trip advisor as stayed at Taj for 3 nights and then thought let me try something new on the way out for one night! Big mistake!
Please go stay at TintAgel for 50 dollars more and it will be an experience to remember!
