title: Ok
text:
We checked in for a 3 night stay at the kingsbury. The staff is nice and friendly, the rooms are old and need refurbishment plus the humidity in the rooms is too high. You can also smell sometimes the odors coming from the AC.
The housekeeping staff passes 2 times everyday, the first time to actually ask you about the occupancy of the room and how many people are staying in that room which we found bizarre and the second to tidy up. 
The morning breakfast has a wide variety of food however not to everyone's morning taste as there's the authentic sri lankan breakfast, the tourists' (that has bread, jam, puffs, danish pastry, croissant etc..) and a salad bar. The tea and coffee area is through pass around. 
The overall experience was okay but the place needs refurbishment

management_response.text:
Dear Tinxy7,

We're extremely sorry you have been given a room in this condition. This is without a doubt a mistake on the part of the hotel as these rooms were under repairs.   

As for the housekeeping rounds, it's a standard practice to do so twice a day. However, with regard to the breakfast buffet, I would like to mention we have fresh juices, cereals, yoghurt varieties, fruits, salads, pickles, cold meats, breads, soups, waffles, pancakes, Indian/Western/Sri Lankan hot breakfast items and two egg stations to briefly wrap up the full spread. Its very unfortunate if you were not satisfied with such an extensive spread. If you would like to share your expectations for breakfast, please do so by writing to me at mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com and we will be more than happy to incorporate your favourites too. This is what makes any establishment a great one when feedback is taken seriously. Thank you for your time.

Please do consider us again if your travels bring you back to Colombo.

With warm regards and best wishes,
Dinithi

title: Event Hotel, rooms need updating
text:
This hotel looks like it's for one thing - weddings. The amenities and restaurants are clearly kitted out for this and there were a number going on during my two night stay.

The rooms are really quite dated, pretty small and not arranged in a particularly efficient manner. It's a huge hotel and the speed of the lifts means you'll want to be on a lower floor although that might be noisy.

The pool is sandwiched between a road and the hotel's car park.

management_response.text:
Dear David L,

The Kingsbury is one of the most sought after hotels for weddings due to its classical elegance, culinary offerings and personalised service. As with most popular hotels, the private functions at times crowd the hotel but this is an opportunity for our foreign guests to witness some traditional Sri Lankan weddings and culture as some of them come with such pomp and pageantry.

We're also sorry to note that rooms decorated in pastel shades of beige, white marble bathrooms with Bvlgari amenities, Italian bed and bath linen were not satisfactory. We hope at least our service was up to you expectation as we would like a second chance at impressing you with our hospitality.

With warm regards and best wishes,
Dinithi

title: Beware of thieves
text: It is not my habit to write a review about an hotel that I was not staying in it, But due to the fact that it not my habit to pay for an hotel without being there , I see myself entitled to do so in this case. And this is the story how it was. We invited through local agent 2 nights at The Kingsbury and payed the full price in advanced. When we got to the hotel we were not impressed neither by the beauty of it nor by the cleaning. But the worst was when we got into the room.The room was located on the fourth floor, it was small and seemed dirty, but worst of all it was entirely opaque glass without having even a small window that can be opened to enable breezing the sea air. It seems to me that every normal human beings staying there getting a sense of the fish in the aquarium, which is not the feeling that I would like to feel in my vacation. Moreover through the frosted glass, we saw the "thrilling" view of entrance and the parking. We immediately started efforts to upgrade the room, if even at all costs. Overall we asked for a room with a balcony or at  least some window that can be opened. But after several calls to the reception it was becoming clear that the only option we offer is a room with a balcony on the 2nd floor just above the entrance of cars, but at the reception they emphasized this option is not recommend. After several failed attempts we realized that in  this hotel we do not have a chance of enjoying and after ninety minutes or so from the moment we arrived to the hotel we found ourselves checking  out without enjoying even a single moment of any service or facility of the hotel. On our way out the manger of the reception desk, emphasized that there is no chance that the money we have paid in advance for two nights will be returned to us, in whole or in part. Perhaps, under the laws of Sri Lanka, the hotel is permitted to take the full payment for 2 nights In which you haven't been there, perhaps, but one thing is clear to me, this is immoral behavior and even from a business point of view it looks bad. This is not a proper behavior from an hotel who considers itself and respects its guests. This is a behavior of one who interested only in money and not in the quality of its services or the wall fare of its guests.

management_response.text:
Dear Moshe S,

We're sorry to note your disappointment and would like to state the following to clarify the situation:

1. The mini aquarium is on the lobby level and we assure you and our guests are a testimony to the fact that there is no 'fishy' smell emanating at all and anyway aquarium fish does not smell as they are live ornamental fish. 

Maybe you are not a fan of ornamental fish and this has in someway, made you uncomfortable. 

2. Most hotels around the world do not have windows or any form of opening for ventilation if the room is air conditioned and in some cases for safety measures. 

However, we have done our best by offering you a balcony room - that has a door to step out into the balcony to enjoy the fresh air and the sea breeze. 

3.Our rooms are maintained according to the highest international standards and we find it hard to believe that they did not look clean, especially since you have not mentioned anything specific its not possible to go beyond this. 

4. Your refund should be requested from the local travel agent, as you have booked and paid them. 
We recommend you try again as we have informed that agent in writing that we will be not charging them for your room. 

Kindly note our cancellation policy is published on our website - www.thekingsburyhotel.com for future reference.
 
Once again, dear guest, we're sorry you could not experience The Kingsbury but we hope you have had the good fortune to enjoy Sri Lanka.

With warm regards and our best wishes!
Dinithi

title: Loud loud loud
text: This is not the best place to stay if you have two small children. We had a room on the 8th floor with a view of the pool. At one point there was incredibly loud music directly above us in addition to music coming from the pool. That's totally fine if you are here to party but I would not recommend staying here if you have children who are trying to sleep. I'm not into the fancy uppity feel but if you do like that kind of thing then I suppose this would be a good place for you. Just not my scene. The staff was nice enough...but I'm looking forward to leaving tomorrow.

management_response.text:
Dear mudithak1982,

This is very unfortunate and please do accept our sincere apologies!  

We would like to find a way of compensating you, please let me know your name and the date you were with us by writing to me at mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com. 

Am sorry you had to leave us this way. If you would reconsider returning to The Kingsbury, we would  ensure your stay is a perfect one.

With warm regards best wishes, 
Dinithi

title: Not 5*
text: Currently staying here. Looks good from outside but having to put up with thumping loud music into the late night/early hours. No room sound proofing. Bad poolside food/drink service. Hotel seems more interested in providing wedding receptions (many per day) than looking after business guests. Wifi slow and patchy.  Below average hotel

management_response.text:
Dear Graham T,

We're extremely sorry to note your experience and please get in touch with me asap as you're currently in-house. This is when we can iron out any shortcomings and ensure your stay is perfect.

My email is mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com or you may have the operators connect you to my mobile from the room phone.

Please be assured we will do everything possible to make your stay a pleasant one.

With warm regards
Dinithi

title: Chaotic, impersonal typical city centre hotel
text:
We visited Sri Lanka for 2 and half weeks and this was the most expensive place we stayed and the most disappointing.
The hotels location in Colombo is good and I suspect it is used by most business people from around the world. This gives it a busy get them in get them out feel.
Everyone in front of us at check out had a complaint about the bill, including us. Hidden taxes charges or services not delivered.
The room was nice but certainly not in tip top condition which you would expect for the price.
Breakfast was nice but there was no service, plates piled up around us and no-one came back to serve us more tea which is the usual at other hotels.
Another guest was actually screaming at staff to get some service, I suspect they had been staying there a while and had had enough of it.
Very disappointing as this was to be a splurge for us but we had way better service and accommodation at places that cost a fifth of what this cost.
Keep looking you can find way better for less.

management_response.text:
Dear DesertDweller10,

We're sincerely sorry your experience at The Kingsbury had not been up to your expectations. Since we're located in the heart of the commercial capital - Colombo, it does make it very attractive for business travellers to stay with us. However our service philosophy is one of 'personalisation' to ensure your meals are perfect and your experiences are timeless, whether you are staying with us on business or leisure. 

With regard to your check-out experience, please note statutory government taxes and service charge must be added to the room rate. These are not hidden taxes or charges for services not delivered. When booking online, we understand that some confusion may arise due to the way some online travel agencies mention deal with the tax component.  

Booking.com - mentions that 25.88% hotel tax is not included
Agoda - mentions that above tax is included but does not give a breakdown
Expedia - clearly shows the tax breakdown in the final booking screen

Finally, your experience at breakfast was a let down and we do apologise. Please be good to provide me (my email: mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com) your check in name and date as we would like to like to compensate you.

We hope your trip Sri Lanka was a memorable one and if you do return, please give us the opportunity to serve you better.

With warm regards and best wishes,
Dinithi

title: Yue Chuan Chinese Restaurant - The Worst Place to Eat in All of Chinese Cuisine
text:
The Kingsbury's so-called Chinese restaurant, Yue Chuan, is an awful establishment.
  When it first opened, about 3 years ago, it was fine, so we decided to go there again today, but ugh, what a wrong choice we made. The food was absolutely rotten - the chef had crazily put almost a full packet of salt into each of our dishes. Also, the green tea tasted as if fish had been inside it! How dreadful this place is! 
  We would definitely not want to come back to this place again in the future, and never, ever, recommend it to anybody seeking to go to a 'Chinese' restaurant.

management_response.text:
Dear Meghana P,

We're extremely sorry you've had such an unpleasant experience at one of our restaurants. In the event had you expressed your dissatisfaction while dining, I can assure you the restaurant staff would have certainly offered you a fresh set of dishes to meet your preferences.

We're very seriously looking into this and we would appreciate if you would get in touch with me at mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com or with our F&B Manager Iyantha Abeysinghe  on fbm@thekingsburyhotel.com to let us know the date you dined with us and what the restaurant staff had offered you in response to your complaint.  

We pride our selves in offering a high level of service and culinary delights that are par excellence. Hence, its genuine feedback that makes its possible for us to maintain such standards. 

We thank you for your time and assure of our attention in this regard.

With warm regards,
Dinithi

title: Average to Good
text: We stayed at this hotel,as we have stayed at most hotels in the area and we wanted something new.The location is really convenient for our business needs,as it is located close to many offices.The staff of the hotel was friendly in general,but we faced some trouble with the room service,as we clearly ordered 2 steak sandwiches and they brought us 2 burgers instead.When we called them to inform that they were mistaken,they said that steaks and burgers are almost the same and they offered to change them but after 30 minutes of waiting.The rooms were very small,but clean in general,although there was a light bad smell around.The bathroom was nice.Even if we stayed at the non smoking  4th floor,there were many people smoking in their rooms,so the smell was really very bad at the corridors,as some clients had most of the day their doors opened,with loud music playing and smoking in and out of the rooms.I am not sure if I will stay again,as my experience with other hotels was better.

management_response.text:
Dear nikolaos v,

Thank you for having chosen The Kingsbury and sharing your experience with us. We regret your stay was marked with a few incidents and please do accept our sincere apologies. 

Room Service division has been addressed to get the order correct the first time instead of offering alternatives or excuses. Smoking in non-smoking rooms we agree is very disrespectful and also is of great discomfort to those who do not. We have taken stringent measures in this regard and we assure you a level of comfort one would expect from a 5 star hotel.

Please let us know the name and date in which you checked in by writing to me at mgrccpr@thekingsburyhotel.com as we would like to further discuss the issues you have stated. 

We wish you the very best and look forward to hearing from you.

With warm regards
Dinithi

title: Not like what you will expect.

it's expensive for nothing.

title: Unbelievable that Non Smoking floor that the guest were Smoking
text:
A very beautiful property but it is unbelievable that when i asked for a Non smoking floor; i was given room 419 which was a Non smoking floor but when i went to the 4th floor which signage show Non Smoking and when the lift open; i could smell cigarette smoke everywhere and a number of the guest room were open with the guest smoking without caring at all. I went to the reception to file a complaint and they change my room to the 8th floor but did not reprimand the guest at all.

title: Worst 'luxury' hotel in Colombo (NO EXAGGERATION) Do not host your function here!
text:
So here's the thing... almost everyone on here has written their review based on one experience. I know when you have an amazing or terrible experience, you just want to let someone know; but my experience with Kingsbury was so disgusting, that I just kept giving the hotel chances, hoping that something would change. IT DIDN'T! My experience is over 1.5 years, and trust me if you are thinking of hosting an event here, my review is a MUST READ!

I have summarised my experiences for all of you.

Early 2013: Made a booking for the Balmoral (Ballroom) for 450-500 pax. I was in constant conversation with a gentleman by the name Rizvi. A couple of months into organising my homecoming (wedding celebration), I realised that nothing was getting done. I went straight to the Banquets team and was told that Rizvi had left the hotel MONTHS AGO!! The guy was taking my calls from home!

Mid 2013: Met with a gentleman by the name Mahesh (who no longer works there). If it wasn't for him, our event would have been a huge flop. He was the only reason we continued to keep our booking at the hotel. He introduced us to the head chef, to help us select our menu. What a waste of time that meeting was. I went through the menu asking him for which food would go with which and he literally said yes to everything, even if i suggested mixing Indian curry with Thai. He was not helpful at all.

Homecoming Day: When I asked for a bottle to be placed on my family table, as the waiters were hopeless, I was told that they couldn't do that unless they got permission. By the way, it is allowed as we bring the alcohol in to the function. Many of our guests later told us that they had to almost scream at staff to get what they wanted, as staff would say "sure" and then never come back!

THE WORST PART: Many of our guests got food poisoning and severely! (we did report this, but not a single person from the hotel commented on it to this day. Since then, we have had many friends say that they too have experienced and heard of many stories of food poisoning at the hotel.

November 2013 - On our Honeymoon: I receive a bank statement on my email which shows that I have been charged for the complimentary suite, which is part of the wedding package. Once we returned back to Sri Lanka, I had weeks of conversations via email and telephone, trying to get my refund. The staff just wouldn't accept that we were overcharged. It took me emailing the GM, to get that refund back. They did send us a cake as an apology.

October 2014: Rung the hotel to find out when we could come for our complimentary 1 year anniversary dinner. Spoke to a one girl at the start (can't remember her name and for several weeks, she kept saying she'd call me back, but never heard from her. I then spoke to a lady by the name Kumarie, who sorted out the voucher for me, but i was sorted a couple of hours from me taking a flight. I informed her that I would pick it up when I return to Sri Lanka in a couple of weeks. I then returned and called the Banquets team, again receiving responses of "we will call you back madam". By this time I was well and truly tired of it, but wanting to pursue this for the purpose of this review. 
Around January, I spoke to a lady by the name Jacqueline who assured me she would get it sorted out, which she did. She gave me her mobile number although never replied when I asked her for the status. I only know she sorted it out because I rung again, extremely annoyed at the situation. Super disappointed that I got a mobile number as assurance, but never a response.

Finally I was so annoyed, I requested to speak to the manager. At first the lady who answered, avoided giving me the manager's number. I was given the Assistant Manager's number - Nishagi. She was the one who finally sorted out this never-ending drama!

Last Night: Called the Harbour Court Restaurant to double check our reservation 3 times. Between each time I called Nishagi to inform her that the staff kept saying there is no reservation under our names. Finally she asked us to ask for Elizabeth who knew about our reservation. Thank you Nishagi for sorting this out for us!

Our experience last night was DISGUSTING! It was 9:30 and the staff were setting up for BREAKFAST!!! The were dragging chairs all over the place, dropping cutlery in buckets etc. It was extremely rude. Our table wasn't even set, when we arrived. They just put down the basic cutlery and kept cleaning. I have a recording of all the noise, which I will be sending the GM.

Finally, when leaving, no one was aware that we didn't have to sign anything....

My Advice to you all: DO NOT host your function here and DO NOT eat at the Harbour Court, especially for dinner. If you want to eat at The Kingsbury, the Chinese Restaurant is amazing and has the most professional and polite staff. The Sky Lounge bar is also very nice.

title: Disappointed
text:
After arriving after a long flight from London, with a transit, at 4am I was told the room would not be available until 12pm.  Understandable if the hotel was fully booked, but of course there were free rooms, at a price (I was told it was a reduced price but a quick check on the Internet proved it was equivalent to booking.com), and in desperation for a bed I paid.  I was astonished to be woken up at 7am on Sunday by building works.  I am very disappointed that the hotel has not advised guests that at the back - seafront end of the hotel - there is a small road, and across it rocks are being moved to create a large building project across a large expanse of the seafront.  The rock moving by heavy earth moving equipment starts at 7am, 7 days a week.  Apart from the awful unexpected wake up call the noise continues throughout the day and effects the whole of the pool area.

My bedroom smelt and felt very damp, probably because the bathroom had no extractor fan to remove the steam.  The bedroom was well appointed therefore it was such a shame that the damp smell pervaded.  As other guests have pointed out, the hotel is gorgeous on the ground floor, but in need of refurbished bedrooms.

The food quality is good, although the breakfast I ordered in my room was stone cold and congealed, and the waiting staff very pleasant.  Prices are good too, however I would not return to this hotel.

title: Whats behind the facade!!
text:
I stayed at the Kingsbury from the 6th until the 12th of February. Although I am a regular visitor to Sri-Lanka this was my first stay at this hotel.
I always have a suites in hotels, this trip being no different. The best available suite was booked.
I had amended my booking 1 week prior to my arrival in SL to include a hotel car transfer from the airport. Upon arrival no car had been arranged. The hotel desk arranged me a local taxi which was cheaper but with no working AC....
The room I had been allocated 500 was extremely dusty, all surfaces when touched were covered in a white dusty film. Upon closer inspection all fixtures and fittings were ground in dirty, clearly the room had not been deep cleaned since it was renovated 2 years earlier.
The duty manager agreed the room was very dirty and gave me room 400 and told it was much better. 
In truth the room was still quite dusty however it was clear an effort had been made (albeit not very well).
The executive lounge on the 9th floor is a joke, its not a lounge at all, its a small room with a few dining tables and chairs, its not a space to relax or feel comfortable in!!! the food and drink provided is also extremely disappointing!
During my stay I noticed the occasional ant in my bedroom, I wasn't really surprised although Ive never seen any insects in any OTHER hotel I've used in colombo.
On the afternoon of the 11th whilst lying in the bath I noticed movement on the bath side and floor below, literally hundreds of ants!!!!
When I challenged the duty manager who came to investigate he suggested that maybe housekeeping could clear them away. I pointed out that pest control would be more appropriate.

Not that the hotel can do anything about it, but be aware of the construction work next door which will last for several years to come, its very noisy, 24hours a day!

The hotel has an impressive facade, thats all..

If anyone asks, I would recommend they stay at the TAJ SAMUDRA, also newly renovated but infinitely better, all round...

Reception service was very poor and we had to wait nearly two hours for our room to be ready. During this time we were given no refreshments and had to keep asking for updates on the readiness of our room. No one kept us informed although we were told they would.
The waiter service by the pool area was good but it was poor and slow in the main restaurant.Even when we sought a manager's assistance, it did not improve. We gave up on trying to get another cup of tea in the end! The quality of the breakfasts was very average for what claims to be a first class hotel.
Staff were keen to make excuses and not remotely apologetic.
The concierge booked us into a really poor restaurant for some Sri Lankan food.
There are a lot of issues in this hotel with regard to customer service. Not a good start to our Sri Lankan trip but all our other hotels so far have been really good.

title: Never again !
text:
Ok, maybe we are a bit spoiled by living in Middle East and having a lot of good hotels around and therefore I usually don't write reviews but this one I need to share with you.
The Kingsbury is boasting 5 stars but deserves maybe 2 or 3 of it. A long sad story…….we arrive and the room is not ready, usually not an issue but the guy at the front desk tries several times to talk me out of the room we had booked. It was an Executive Suite with Sea View – not that the sea view was nice at all (huge construction site where the beach used to be) but I wanted to have it, since I paid for it and only once I told him a piece of my mind he agreed but made us wait 2 hours for that…..and that’s only how it started.
The room was nice though it had seen better days, we were on the 5th floor – luckily, because on the 10th is a party hall for private events which seems to be booked daily with music until after midnight and we could still sing along even 5 floors lower.
The breakfast was another eye opener…..the waiters are absolutely inattentive, usually talk among each other together with their supervisors and need encouragement to bring some coffee or tea. The uniforms look like they get to the laundry twice a year and the whole atmosphere is anything but hospitable. The overall food choice and presentation is nice with average quality.
Included in our room package was a daily fruit basket and chocolates……we called 5 times until we got one apple, a few grapes and 2 pieces of chocolate and only after I requested the Manager on duty and complained officially we received what we paid for…..but only one time….after that it stopped completely.
The doormen are as unfriendly as the other staff but are surely business-minded. They will offer you immediately to call a “friend” to give you a ride somewhere for a very good rate…..which turns out to be twice as much than you would pay usually.
Here and there you will find attentive and caring people, the executive lounge for example has some really friendly and kind staff, the lounge itself I will better not mention here…..
The “Ocean” sea food place is the only highlight in the complete shop. Excellent food and wine, lovely presentation and truly attentive and caring staff – that was a real 5-Star experience, the rest sadly but truly was crap .We have come to Sri Lanka regularly for 20 years and have stayed in a lot of excellent hotels that deserve 5 stars but The Kingsbury is surely not among such ones and we will never go back there.

title: Nice hotel but.....
text:
We stayed at the Kingsbury for the first two nights of our stay in Sri Lanka and whilst the room was comfortable, and the hotel clean and efficient, a few things have left a bad taste in my mouth.

We ordered a minibus to take us to our next hotel (we are an extended family on holiday so had 3 or 4 rooms booked) which never arrived, I was double charged for Shisha in the pool bar (and the server insisted on closing the bill as it was the end of his shift, even though we were staying at the pool bar and the rest of our family were coming and going) and now in hindsight I think the staff also tried to 'forget' to give us our change for our spend there - or at least when I remembered that I was owed change, they were hugely unsurprised.

In short, as long as you keep your wits about you and don't trust anyone or relax at all (though, that kind of defeats the object of being on holiday in a 5* hotel doesn't it??) the Kingsbury is great. 
I would also recommend checking the room out first if you can, our 'great pool and partial sea view' was actually a view of their carpark and a construction site. 
(Breakfast was good though, think that was a highlight!)

The service is good, particularly in the Sky Lounge and The Café, less so in the restaurant and at reception. Rooms are clean and spacious, the bathrooms well appointed. Food quality is good. I was collected at the airport and returned to the airport by the hotel - marked differences, the inbound trip was fantastic, the outbound trip terrible - the car had a major shudder at anything over 70kph, the driver (at 03h00) seemed on the verge of falling asleep and spent most of the trip wandering from lane to lane without and regard for traffic behind, indicator left on virtually the whole way. With the Hilton and Cinnamon Lakeside virtually next door, the Kingsbury has major competition who offer more at comparable prices.

title: Not recommending for a wedding!!
text:
I had my wedding, a Sri Lankan wedding this month at Kingsbusy, I got the worst service ever. 
Starting from the coordinator,he was no use at all, he was never reachable via phone and had disappeared on event day. The things I had coordinated to him wasn't  coordinated to other hotel staff. 
My wedding was an evening wedding and event was supposed to start at 6pm. There was a wedding going on in the morning, in the same hall and they had promised to clean the hall and handover to my deco people at 4.30. Even at 6.15 they were cleaning and putting seat covers, and my guests were standing and watching. Hotel staff didn't make any effort to make it quick or to put more staff, they were just doing it on their usual speed, leisurely like my wedding had no importance.
The setty back and other stuff from the previous wedding was just at the entrance of the hall, even at 6.30. So my parents and guests had to move them their-selves because it seemed be useless to talk to the hotel staff for support. My registration was supposed be at 6.43 and even at 6.35 they hadn't put a table for that. The answer my family got continuously was ,they are under staff due to another wedding going on in the ground floor, Is it really my problem???? I paid the same amount for the service, hotel knew that there going to be another wedding and still didn't make any effort to make it fair for both weddings.
It looked like the staff who was at service was just trainees. During the toast they had forgotten to serve wine to the couple. And during the dinner, they wanted my husband to pay Rs 750 because one of our friends had ordered some drinks. Seriously ??? A Rs 750 bill to groom during the dinner in front of all guests??
My wedding could be a just another event for the hotel, but for us it's life time event. For any couple it is a life time memory. And no couple expect such pressure on their big day. Hotel staff has  a "responsibility". Because the poor service of the hotel, we couldn't follow any Nakath time.
Now I regret for choosing Kingsbury for my wedding. And will never ever recommend for any one.

title: Most comfortable bed EVER.... But could never catch a lift !
text:
My partner and I recently stayed in The Kingsbury as part of our tour in Sri Lanka. On arrival we were very impressed with the hotel; the lobby was decorated in grand fashion and the rooms were well appointed, modern and clean. The floor to ceiling window provided a lovely view of the sun setting over the sea. But by far my favourite thing in the room was the bed which I struggled to get out of in the morning! 

We enjoyed the use of the pool and gym facilities which were both well appointed however the building site at the end of the "infinity pool" was a bit unsightly. That was of course when we could get downstairs ... The hotel's two lifts (for an averagely large hotel...nowhere near enough) were infuriatingly slow and most often skipped our floor, with no stairs we had no option but to wait. The food in the hotel left a lot to be desired ... The breakfast was awful! Like most hotels we had stayed in the eggs station was cooked in front of you as well as bacon and sausages - this novelty had worn off and the result was omelettes resembling scrambled eggs half cooked sausages and soggy bacon. I would much prefer this to be cooked in bulk and be properly cooked! My partner bit into the sausage which was stone cold!!! 

I would recommend staying at this hotel but go elsewhere for food!

title: Good hotel with extremely bad service!
text:
The hotel is situated beach side and has newly renovated rooms that are a delight. Rooms overlook two different views. One view is of the city and the beach while the other is of the beach and of the port. Some of the corner suites have both these views and I do recommend that you stay in the suite. Generally the rooms size must be close to about 350 square feet but the suite is much bigger and should be around 550 square feet.
The food at the hotel is excellent. The breakfast is diverse with a egg station, a fantastic sausage and bacon station, Indian breakfast items like idli, medhu wada, dosa, and they also serve the traditional Sri Lankan breakfast. Overall a fantastic spread. The only problem is that they should have at least two egg stations instead of one. The reason is that you cannot give your order and go and sit down waiting for them to get it. You have to stand in the line here to get it and the line gets pretty lengthy at time.
The ground floor reception, the pool, the skybar, the bathrooms, everything in this hotel including the buffet is really good. What this hotel lacks is service! They have absolutely NO CONCEPT of good service. Three hotels are coming up just next to the Kingsbury- The Grand Hyatt, The Shangrila,and the ITC Grand Maratha. I think there are also plans for another Hilton to come up there. Already existing are the Hilton and the Taj Samudra among the good hotels near the Kingsbury. With this level of competition, the Kingsbury cannot afford this level of service. They need a CEO for the hotel who has taken care of a five star hotel of excellent repute as far as service goes.
Overall, even with everything being so good, because of the terrible service, I am giving it a two out of five.

text: True that kingsbury is a nice fancy hotel. but i recently had a very bad experience. we were invited to a wedding at kingsbury a couple of days back. my husband and i got there around 8.30pm and the place was crowded. A nice fancy Porsche came, owner got off, gave the key to the security guard and nicely walked in. we also asked if we could give the car for vale parking but the guard said we'll have to go park in the parking lot. no offence, we went down to the parking lot as guided by the guard. spent about 10 minutes looking for a place to park, but couldn't find. then a guard guided us through a gate (which i thought another section of the parking lot) which lead us to the road. Then we thought we'll park in the side of the road and walk all the way to the hotel. when we were parking in the road, a navy personnel came, tapped on to the window. asked where we are heading to. said its to the hotel. Then he snapped at us saying don't you know this not the hotel parking and you are not suppose to park. we didn't want to make a scene so we  moved the car and went back to the hotel again. we talked to same guard and said there was no parking.. then he showed a small corner towards the road and asked to park. however i saw some empty places for parking near the entrance. never mind though, we moved the car to the far corner he showed. with great effort, we manged to fit the car in to the tiny spot. the minute we both got off the car, a police officer came and said the we have parked in the pavement and to move the car. my husband got mad and said we'll ditch the wedding and go home. i said we'll go back in cz i saw some empty spots for parking. we went back to the hotel and parked in a vacant spot near the entrance with the fancy cars.. the same guard came running to the car saying you cant park here. i got soooo mad that i got off the car and asked him "who do you think we are? 2 beggars? why cant we park here? if a fancy car can park here why not us. true our car is old and not fancy. true we are not so rich and mighty. but we should be treated equally." then he let us park in that spot. so with shouting at the guard only we could get a parking spot. anyway i felt so discriminated and cheap. i have never been treated like that ever in my life. it hit me that we were treated differently. anyways it was 9.30 when we got to the wedding hall(1 hour later) after the great struggle of finding a parking spot..

title: Poor service on a building site. Not somewhere for a family holiday.
text:
Quite frankly – where do you start with this one.

Checked in for 5 nights, only stopped two. 

Not very good at all and I’d avoid at all costs.

Firstly, with the exception of the concierge and the cleaners, the service level is appalling.  I put this down in a large part to the fact that service charge is automatically added to everything so nobody is working for tips.  There also seem to be far too many people walking around in suits, proud of themselves that they have some junior management role/work in a supervisory capacity, clicking their fingers at the poor staff who are not enough in number.  Maybe if they were to pull their fingers out then things would be better.  However the arrogance of the suit seems to work against them.

Service is slow in the restaurant, but don’t worry, whilst you wait you can entertain yourself by watching the man with an electric tennis racquet walk around killing flies.

The big problem for me is that the hotel is now smack bang on a building site.  The sea views have all but gone and the noise is terrible.  I take severe issue with this as their website still portrays an infinity pool overlooking the sea.  You’ll see from my pictures that it really doesn’t!  The description is one of being able to relax in tranquil environments and peace.  Again, unless you are deaf that is not going to happen.

What makes it worse is that I spoke to the general manager – Mr Maurice Cook – who told me the website would be changed.  It hasn’t.  What makes it laughable is that he said “we advertise an infinity pool and that’s what there is” NO you advertise an infinity pool overlooking the ocean in a tranquil environment.  IT IS NOT.  In the UK that would be mis-advertising and illegal.

I feel sorry for the hotel that it has been ruined by building work, but we made the decision to stay here on this basis and they deny any problems.  Simply unacceptable and it is treating guests with contempt. 

So problems started when we arrived to check in.  No rooms were ready – it had only been booked for 14 months so we were probably a surprise!  When we eventually went to the room it stank of cigarette smoke and they hadn’t erected the second bed we needed for the boys.

After complaining we were moved to another room – but first of all this needed to be cleaned (I have to say the cleaners on floor 5 were the only saving grace to this hotel).  It was eventually cleaned but they forgot the other bed!  We were told to come back in half an hour (we’d already been at the hotel 2 hours!) when we came back still no bed!  It eventually got sorted but it was a palaver.

The rooms themselves are very clean, but they are just a bit shabby for the money you are paying.  Unlike other hotels we stayed in of a similar quality whilst in sri lanka, television for children was poor and there was no DVD player.  The view was not great – fortunately we had the side not overlooking the pool / construction site, but the roof of the hotel looks ugly.  Not what is shown in the brochure.

Food quality was good – but average for an establishment like that.  Prices comparatively high.  They seem reasonable but then they add the tax and service charge and it is not so good.  Vegetarian options more limited than in other hotels but the breakfast was good.  Only issue was they kept running out of cutlery and bowls so people were left waiting and it became bothersome.  Finding a clean table in the morning was also difficult - more chance of seeign a suited finger clicker!  

It was all just rather an inhospitable welcome and not at all pleasant.  The area it is in within Colombo is not too nice either.  We ventured out a few times, but avoid the hotel transport desk unless you don’t mind being fleeced for a journey.  Speak to the concierge people instead.  Saved about £50 on transport just by chatting to them.
	
I’d personally spend a maximum of 1 day in Colombo anyway (we moved to more of a beach location).  This hotel is not for families wishing to relax and enjoy the country.

Really not very good – hold themselves up to be a cut above, the reality is they can’t make the grade and actually embarrass the Sri Lankan hospitality we received elsewhere.  We checked out early and were thankful for it.  Although to be fair Mr Cook did see us off and refunded a night's stay.  But it really did leave a sour ending to the whole holiday.

Opted to give it poor rating rather than terrible rating, because it was clean – and so it could have been worse.

Plenty of other options.  I’m not one for warning people off but I would highly recommend another hotel.

title: totally overstated
text:
They apply (almost) international prices but quality, unfortunately, does not follow. Speaking about rooms, what they call a suite is just a big room with a sofa and two armchairs. Forget about separated living room....
Do not get fooled by pictures from their website: from the pool, you have a fantastic view onto a big pile of grey rocks that totally blocks any view you might want to have of the sea, from the "sea view corner suite" as they call it you have unabashed views over concrete platforms overlooking an industrial area. Let's not speak about decoration made out of cheap furniture.
Add to that the fact today they are hosting two big weddings, most of the restaurants are off limit, the noise level in the lobby is unbelievable, with only two elevators at hand, you have no solution other than taking the stairs. All in all, It is a sheer nightmare. Ah, I forgot to mention that all around work is in progress in surrounding building developments so, if you are keen onto drilling, hammering, etc noises, you might enjoy the pool area.
Reception desk is crowded at all times (not by staff!) and any basic enquiry takes ages.

title: What poor management is about...
text:
I had to stay 5 days at the Kingsbury and honestly I took some times before to book because the hotel infrastructures in Colombo are not great due to lack of investment during the last 20 years. So hotels are usually old. Hopefully they are now building 10 new hotels and soon the Shangri La and the Hyatt will open. I thought the Kingsbury was one of them as newly renovated. To summarise:

Good things: rooms are well renovated. Bed is comfortable .Bathrooms well designed. Big window. Nice location in front of the sea. The pool area. The food.

Bad things: do not look at the details as the renovation has been made quickly. The lobby is busy, noisy with good buffets all around making the impression we are in court food rather than an hotel. Do not book a room at the executive floor as you will be underneath of the disco and you will hear music half of the night. Do not ask anything as if you want to book a restaurant in town, she will ask you the phone number, dial it and pass you the phone to talk directly to them to confirm your reservation! Do not ask for a taxi, otherwise the bell boy will book you am hotel car at prohibitive cost and if you challenge him he will explain that they have received the instruction from their manager not to call public taxis (which are new Toyota Eco Hybrid with meter and not expensive at all). Do not go to the hair dresser as the place smell bad due to lack of aeration. Do not use the gym as everybody in the street can see you sweating and all Spa Staff and Gym Trainers are watching TV there. 

This is a real shame as this place could be great with a strong management and a minimum of good taste!

Not recommended at all.
