title: Well beyond "teething problems"
text: Spent 4 nights here in early April.  Still too many problems for a hotel that has been open for several months.  A sample: (a) the idea that guests might want coffee or tea with breakfast seems like a completely novel concept to staff in restaurant --- 10-15 minute wait every morning, even when not at all crowded and numerous staff wandering around in an apparent fog. (b)  "Do not disturb" sign in rooms impossible to find --- so subject to numerous disruptions by staff at all hours of day and night;  (c) Gym smelt like a broken sewer line, and had been set up by clueless people -- eg, treadmills had not been leveled; (d) checking-out takes forever --- even when I asked the reception staff to hurry up (after a 15 minute delay), the last guy insisted on wasting even more time folding and refolding a single leaf of paper, even when I insisted I do that myself!  And car we had booked through hotel to airport insisted they had no room for luggage(!) so 3 people had to pay for 2 cars, and then drivers delayed departure trying to sort out confusion with reception over how they would be paid for cars charged to rooms!  Multiple and basic problems of these kinds suggest the issue extends far beyond "teething problems" -- they constitute a fundamental failure of management.

title: If you want a hotel experience to forget, this is the place
text:
Stayed at the hotel with our children and friends plus their children (8 of us in total). All up we had 4 rooms booked. Despite far more staff behind the reception desk than customers in front of it, still managed to take them over 30 minutes to complete simple check in process. Managed to get 2 rooms on same floor for us and our kids (despite the special request for adjoining rooms). Our friends did manage to get adjoining rooms, many hours after check in despite assurances all would be ready within 30 minutes.
Had an early dinner with our friends at Kings restaurant. They managed to get 4 of the 7 orders correct when they served our meal after 45 minutes (we were the only ones in the restaurant at that time). It then took a further 40 minutes for the correct meals to come out. We then had to stand with the manager to tell him what we ordered for dinner. 
Despite setting the air system to 23 before we went to dinner, the temperature was 29 when we arrived back at 9pm and stayed that temp all night despite setting the thermastat to 20. Further, there was no soap or shampoo in the room..the list goes on.
We ordered a snack from the hotel cafe 40 minutes before departing for airport. We needed to chase them constantly. The meals arrived 40 minutes later, when we needed to depart (including the pre made tandori chicken wrap sitting behind the counter)...
Only redeeming features are quality of bed and nice pool but not enough to overcome the terrible service. Will never be back.

title: Second visit was a big letdown
text:
First visit to Harbour Court dinner buffet on 16 February 2013 was very enjoyable. We were so satisfied we thought we should go for a second visit  

Second visit on 30 March was a disaster. The quality, variety and the taste had dropped drastically. In the first visit the grill section had prawns and salmon, etc. On the second visit no prawns even though the hotels boasts that it is surrounded by the sea. For sea food there was only rubbery cuttlefish and two varities of  local fish. The same rubbery cuttlefish was offered at the Chinese action station, that was practically impossible to chew. The pasta we tried was unseasoned and the chef who prepared it used the smoked salmon and mushrooms sparingly. The quality of desserts were quite ordinary.

title: Great views but not much else....
text:
This hotel is not ready for occupancy, they need at least six more months to get pretty much everything ready.....

The staff needs to be trained better, the housekeeping staff need a whole lot of help...even the parking lot (more like what parking lot!) is not even close to being ready.

Service takes forever.

The lobby area is kinda stark and weird..with huge black chairs being placed along the walls. The bar though large and open needs much better trained staff, same with their coffee shop.

The totally out-of-place aquarium tower (WTF) had a new dead fish in it every day I was there. It may be cleaned regularly but it looks dirty constantly.   

The mirror in the elevator is already staining, at least one floor tile in each room/bathroom/restaurant I visited was damaged. The glass panels in the restaurants weren't cleaned, the beading/caulking was already coming off.

And please disable or prevent the lifts from stopping at floors that are still under construction.

The buffet is very good, great selection, good quality. The layout is a little dodgy cuz you unless you look really hard, you may end up missing some of the choices on offer.

The chef's at the action stations need better training. Most times there wasn't anyone manning the stations and when they were, they had a hard time grasping spicy, not spicy, rare, medium etc., and the action stations take forever. The hotel may want to consider table service once you place the order. 

The chef at the crepe station didn't know how to make a crepe!

The pool area is fabulous. Awesome views.

The seafood restaurant needs a whole lot of work.

Overall, this place needs more time to get their act together, if/once they do, the hotel has great promise and potential.

title: I got really mad!
text:
There is an enormous space for improvement: 
1. I booked via their website, they gave me a rate, I confirmed with my cc details...and never heard anything again. So I e.mailed, no answer.  I called, no information. Eventually I talked to the front desk manager, then I got a confirmation. But unfortunately to a much higher price. 
Not nice. Took hours to finalize the booking.

2. Finally I arrived. I had asked in my confirmation for a quiet room. Sure enough, they offered me the closest room towards a busy street on the lowest available level.  Thank god to the kind gentlemen from the reception, I got a fine room on a higher floor. I slept well. The rooms are small but ok, light colors, I am not sure what they will look like in one year. 
Food and Wine was good by the way, the terrace a pleasure and the service pretty good.

3. They had not mentioned once in their conformation that the pool has not opened yet. 
They said they did  but I checked all my mails...nothing.

And finally the reason I got mad: 

4. Across the street, the entire concrete garbage, probably from the old pool, was dumped into the ocean. I ask the security person on the street why that was, he said,  oh do not worry, they remove it again. The next day they did, they took a digger and pushed it further in. I complained at the reception, they said, oh its not ours. But my translator talked again to the security on the street and they said of course it is.
What a sad thing to do. Don't they know that nature is the highest gift they have? 
I know that environment protection has not been a huge issue on the island, but I expect this from a expensive Hotel company. There has to be a start somewhere!

Once everything is finished and done I am sure the place will be ok, the stuff certainly is but I can not accept nor understand dumping construction waste into the ocean and I hope many people who read this feel the same.

With regard to the your last point - dumping construction waste into the ocean, we would like to categorically state that The Kingsbury has not at any given time, ever, dumped any waste into the ocean nor does the pile of waste by the ocean belong to The Kingsbury. The security person who had told you that the wast belongs to the hotel is seriously mistaken. 

We do apologise for your pain of mind in this regard and assure you that the environment and 'Green' practices are of paramount importance to us at all times.

title: Food is amazing , staff not so much
text:
We went for the lunch buffet at kingsbury last week and it was simply fabulous.  There was a vast spread of dishes to suit any taste and preference. The staff at harbour court restaurant was friendly and efficient.  
Our wedding was also held at kingsbury last December and although the food was excellent we can't say the same about their service.  Every time we went to meet the coordinator she acted as if it's our first visit and we ended up giving the same information repeatedly. Also, as we were given a room in another hotel the coordinator assured that transportation will be arranged. However we ended up paying for the transportation they arranged and this was not reimbursed.  Furthemore, as our wedding package was platinum category we are entitled to 2 lunch or dinner vouchers which we still haven't received ,although our wedding was held almost  3 months ago.  And when inquired the coordinator told that one of the vouchers is actually the lunch we had during the wedding for which obviously we had already paid. 
So  although the food at kingsbury is delightful their staff and service need a lot of improvement. It's a great venue for a wedding as the buffet is excellent, that is if you're willing to go through a lot of inconveniences.

title: 5 Star comfort, 2 star service
text:
I booked my stay in the hotel online, clicking YES on the airport pickup - after all, I had a pretty late flight in and figured the convenience of them picking me up was worth the price. Until I got to the meeting point and no one was there for me. Yes - they forgot me. 

Thankfully, the guy from the Hilton was around, and he sorted me out with a solution to the hotel.

When I arrived, I mentioned that they had forgotten my transfer, so they asked to see my reservation, and plain to see was the "Airport Pickup - Yes". They may have mumbled an inaudible apology.

They gave me an internet code so that I could send the e-mail confirmation to their manager. The internet code didn't work. When I tried to phone downstairs to tell them, the phone also did not work. This, then, was not a good start.

Finally all this was sorted out and I decided I needed some food from room service. I ordered local food, and it arrived punctually - great taste but the portions a little small, with the exception of the bread which must have used half the wheat crop of the USA, and most of Europe's butter mountain.

The rooms themselves are spacious, the bed big enough to land an A380 on, and very comfortable. Even in the rooms without the view, there is a view of the ocean, although you don't quite get to experience the splendour of the Sri Lankan sunset.

For breakfast there is a massive selection of food, some amazing truly freshly squeezed fruit juices. Personally I like Sri Lankan curry for breakfast, so I was a little disappointed that there were only 2 on offer. Still, excellent flavours, but could have done with a little more variety.

Another thing that bugged me was this: the mini bar is stocked nicely with a decent selection of drinks. Coke, Sprite and San Pelegrino though are all cap bottles. Is there a bottle opener in the room? No. What you have to do is call guest services and get the one guy from the hotel with a bottle opener to come and open your bottle. Every time. I tried it - I drank my Coke. 15 minutes later, I called him up again for the Sprite. Then I waited an hour before I called up so I could drink the water. 

220 rooms, 1 bottle opener. 

The hotel DID give me a free transfer to the airport to make up for the fact that they had forgotten my arrival. But I had to request it - it was not something that they thought of.

Finally - there is a guy playing music in the bar on the ground floor. He is awesome.

title: Great view ! Bad choice for food !
text:
The hotel looks fab from the outside creating very high expectations. However the small lobby area and the restaurants make the place look very overcrowded. The circular pillar salt aquarium looks fab and well fitting into the theme of a sea side hotel.
The lunch buffet sadly is average. The large variety of salads and dessert hardly makes up for the extremely poor selection of the main course. I guess it is a good idea to have action stations and a chef to prepare food to your liking but however this is insanity for a lunch buffet , especially when there is a large crowd . After all you dont come to spend the whole day at the lunch buffet. The chefs are pleasent and helpfull but this does not make up for not getting the dish you ordered. There was a large crowd and the chef told me he will send me my order to the table but it NEVER came.

Overall staff are hrlpfull and try there best but need a lot more practise to sound genuine. I would probably not visit a second time for the lunch buffet as its not value for money. After all did not pay so mucn to eat salad and dessert!

title: Very elegant hotel but poor service
text:
The hotel is still under construction. But have reopened with total elegant interior atmosphere. I chosed this hotel for my wedding as it was reopened & I loved the fresh of it. But unfortunately the service has not reach to see as a one of 5 star or 4 star level hotels in the capital of Colombo. Really good food, good rooms & friendly staff but with poor knowledge.

Service staffs are not capable to deliver the guest requirements. We were with some of our family friends who came down for the wedding from Netherlands. We are not happy with the experience they had during their stay. The b/fast order took 1 & 1/2 hrs to serve & it has served with wrong items. We ordered one sweet wine & the supervisor don’t know what’s the meaning of sweet wine is & it was embarrassed. Their room view was towards to the pool which is on construction & we feel really sorry about our friends. We met couple of managers in order to inform them about the poor service we received. These type of impressions can be damaged to the industry. Houskeeping didn't worry to refresh the room.  

The dinner order came with full of wet napkins. Luckily had enough tissues in the room to wipe our hands. They Banquet team was well supported in coordinating things. Rizvi & chef team did a really good work.

title: Not Ready!
text: Yes, it is a beautiful hotel in a beatiful location with wonderful views and good staff. Restaurants and bar look good, and there rooms although not very big are very tastefully and thoughtfully done. Very Beautiful. BUT, make no mistake it is not ready, and it will not be ready for several months! We didn't stay but had a thorough tour, checked both suites as well ad standard rooms. Only two floors are in operation at the moment, all others are still under construction. We went on a saturday, and there was construction noise even then. There is no pool, no other sports facilities or parking as all of that is still a construction site! The staff said that the pool is supposed to open in two months (April 2013), but how reliable that is remains to be seen. If I was staying at this hotel, I would feel robbed as there are no facilities, not even all the restaurants are open. yet there is no discount. I'm sure when it is ready it will be wonderful, but make sure it is completed before you plan on staying here.

text:
who was the person behind in decorating the lobby , no taste and no concept behind it, we were disappointed when we walked in.

title: Romeo Suite was nice
text: Not what we expected, the room was very nice had beautiful veiws of the ocean altho the rooms had no balcony, the location was close enough to airport as we only stayed in Sri Lanka one night as a stop over to get to the Maldives, the food made me sick The following day, the hotel staff were not very friendly over all we would not stay at this hotel again.

title: Pleasant hotel
text: This hotel is well located for seeing colombo's top sights. The staff are friendly. The decor could do with some modernising

title: A blast from the past.
text:
I had a quick one night stay in this hotel on 2 separate occiasion in the same month.
A few other people have spoken about how old the hotel is, in respect to its fixtures and fittings etc'. Well, I also found this, but for me it made the stay all the more interesting. It was like being in a bit of a time warp which I rather enjoyed.
The room itself was very basic, but functional for what I needed (sleep and a bit of relaxation).
The food in the restaurant was excellent with very helpful waiting staff, and even better food.
Just watch out for the call asking if you want a massage though!!!! LOL

title: comfortable but overpriced hotel
text:
If this hotel were a 3 star, and the price you were paying was for a 3 star, it would be fine, I'd have been happy. But you pay here for a 5 star, and it's not even close to a 5 star. Everything is old and not renovated in the Ceylon Continental: lobby, toilets, elevator, furniture in bedrooms, curtains, swimming pool (very bad maintenance). 
The people working there are very nice, that's the best thing. Food in the restaurant is nice. And the view from my room was great.
Overall, you are paying much more than the hotel deserves.

title: Not a very pleasant memory
text:
I stayed in this hotel in may 2009. It came to my mind to review it now while i was browsing some of the pictures of this colombo buisness trip.

I don't hold very fond memories of this hotel as i got food poisoned and i fell sick accordingly for most of the duration of my trip. I don't what is exactly what i ate that caused this poisoning but i hadn't eaten anything outside the hotel. I've used the restaurant overlooking the ocean and the following night i have used the indian restaurant and in the morning the main restaurant where i had breakfast then after few hours i fell sick :(

I have no complaints about the beds or the room itself. My room was overlooking the ocean but the windows were closed with a sign that it is forbidden to open them.
There are two many weddings in this hotel and if you live next to the bride and groom's bedroom, your life won't be so easy because they keep getting visitors all the time that mainly cause a loud noise because they are usually many!

i would have recommended this hotel for a buisness trip but the food poisoning that happened to me makes it hard for me to recommend the hotel.

title: Old Property
text:
This is a very old property but very well located right on the sea side. One can see the harbour from the pool area where the light house would amaze your kids. The food of the restaurant was very nice and A la carte menu was not expensive.

The rooms were comparatively small with a very small bathroom.

The famous Indian restaurant of the hotel is closed for renovation.

title: Overpriced
text: The whole hotel looks like it will need a good makeover - it still looks like in the 1970s. This dated look includes the hotel lobby, the lift and especially the room and bathroom. The furniture, TV and bed in the room is in a horrible condition - old and tired looking. The bathroom is really small and it is in a horrible state - moldy and rusty. I cannot believe the hotel actually charged guests USD230++ a night and it is rated 5 star. The only plus point i can think of is the northern indian cuisine restaurant in the hotel which served some excellent food.

title: Definitely not a five star..an Average hotel
text:
This hotel i guess is the oldest 5 star hotel in Colombo. Not very well maintained and staff are anything but courteous. The food was very ordinary and service average. However something that was at par with the best hotel in Srilanka was the tariff.

The best thing about this hotel was the location.

title: A reasonable hotel in a good location in Colombo.
text:
Summary:
Ceylon Continental Hotel is a reasonable hotel in a good location in Colombo.

Arriving at Ceylon Continental Hotel:
My company booked the room and had arranged with the hotel for an airport pick-up.  The driver was waiting for me at the airport arrivals and we were soon on the way to the hotel.  Traffic permitting, it's about a 40 minute drive.  Check-in was fine.  As there is no free wi-fi, I bought a 7 day access card from the business centre at the same time.  This proved to be a very good idea.

Ceylon Continental Hotel itself:
When it opened, this was the first 5-star hotel in Colombo - and it used to be an InterContinental. The location is good, being right on the coast and Galle Face Green.  While the public areas are still very nice, the rooms are long overdue for a major renovation and could no longer be considered 5 star.   The pool area is very nice.   Staff are very friendly and helpful. 

Rooms:
Most rooms will have sea views.  Standard rooms are not very large and are in need of a renovation.  But they are comfortable enough, except for being a bit noisy (you can hear any conversations in the hallway) at times.  The bathroom is small.   A newspaper is delivered each morning.
 
Meals:
The buffet breakfast is very good.  I tried room service a couple of times for dinner and found it fine.  The downstairs bar has happy hours each day and quite a good bar menu.  On the weekend evenings the whole downstairs bar and public areas transform into quite a night-club scene!

Leaving Ceylon Continental Hotel:
Check-out was quick and simple and the hotel arranged my transport to the airport.

title: Outdated & Overpriced
text: Stepping into the lobby I felt kind of indifferent about the place.  I didn't realise what it was until I stepped onto their elevator and walked through the hallway to my room.  The place was nice and clean but the interiors looked like one of the first hotels I stayed in 20 years ago.  The room itself was big enough for me but the drab feeling extended into it from the hallway.  The furniture looked old with a tv that felt the same way.  The bathroom was clean but the design was poor.  For the price I had to pay I really expected better than this.  The pool was less than welcoming considering that there was nobody swimming in it and it was too blue for my taste that I felt something wrong with it.  Nevertheless the food at the restaurant inside was great but then again I only had breakfast there.  All in all the service that the whole staff provided was good and you can see that they're eager to please the guest but there is only so much they can do in a place that seemed left behind in the 80's.

title: A business hotel, but not bad
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel in both an arrival and departure from Sri Lanka. We were not that impressed when we first arrived, but the room was big and had a great view of Colombo. Our second stay was a different matter. The previous two nights we spent at the truly awful 'Villa Ocean View' in Wadduwa, so our arrival back into Colombo was a huge relief.
The staff were always friendly and efficient and the rooms were clean. 
Would stay here again.

title: Good Location, but in need of a refurbishment
text:
Stayed here for a weekend while in the city for a family event. Chose this hotel sue to it's proximity to some other events all happening in the vicinity. 
Used their airport pickup, which was pretty smooth. On checking-in, found the rooms to be a bit small and the decor seemed a little dated. Not too the point where things were run-down, but just looked a little past it's time. 
Service was pretty good right thru. Most of the rooms come with some sea-view of sorts. Either you'd be facing the port, else you'd be facing Galle road, which gives you more of a city view. 
   From what i gather, the hotel now is undertaking a refurbishment and so it should be pretty neat once that exercise is complete.

title: Musty, overpriced, no longer 5 star
text:
I opted to stay here due to proximity to meetings in the Fort. But for $185 a night, it is not worth it. The rooms are musty, pillows are hard, breakfast buffet is sub-standard (eg canned sweetened juices, no fresh). Altogether a bit tired, and certainly not worth the money. For business purposes in Colombo, the Cinnamon hotels are so much better in every respect,  
except  for the outrageous charges for WifI!

title: never be back
text:
entry of the hotel is huge, nice and pleasant, but none of the staff....it seems they had to be forced to make a smile.
Disaster started with the first selection of room, after specifically asking for the sea view room, it was not given, had to change room twice as 2nd one which was offered was not clean enough and some of the facilities like channel music, TV and tea kettle was was not working, seems like all rooms in hotel needs a renovation and change of cutlery also.
Though the breakfast had a lot of choices specially the local dishes were in large number, so if you are specific about your breakfast better stick to non local dishes.
though decided no more stay back in that property anymore.

title: Great location, but slightly dated hotel with scope for improvement.
text: The Ceylon continental is ideally located, in the heart of the city, by the sea. The hotel is a little old fashioned in terms of its decor and overall look. Rooms are small, but comfortable and clean and offer a nice view of the sea. The food served at the restaurants is average, mainly local cuisine, but not very well made. Staff are friendly and helpful. The nicest part is the wonderful view of the sea and the location.

title: Would prefer Hilton and the Taj instead in Colombo
text: Ceylon Continental is one of the oldest star hotel in Colombo, which still shows in some of the hospitality services. I was stunned to see that they still use the archaic system of keeping room keys in the hotel. I have never seen this with any other quality hotel in the sub-continent. The food is just OK and I had to walk down to the nearby Hilton Hotel to enjoy the breakfast buffet. I belive there is lot of scope in terms of imrpovement of facilities. Even room service needs to improve. The only advantage is the beachline location and proximity to the Galadhari hotel, Taj samudra and the Hilton. I will advise people to visit Hilton and other quality hotels in Colombo

title: 5* prices for 3* quality
text:
I recently stayed here during the Cricket World Cup. Therefore I expected the hotel room rates to be a bit higher than during an off-peak season. Other hotels in the area were also charging up, which is fine - make hay whilst the sun is shining I suppose. However I was very disappointed to be charged 5* rates (USD200-250) per night for a 3* quality hotel. Part of this was my fault, in hindsight I should have probably pushed my travel agent a bit but I booked last minute and I really wanted to visit Colombo to attend one of the matches so I didn't push hard enough. I found out later from other guests that they were paying USD130-175 per night.

Anyway to the crux of the story - this is definitely a hotel that has long seen its glory days. It is badly in need for a complete renovation. The rooms are old, the bathrooms are even worse. The sofa was dirty as were the towels. The hotel lobby needs a re-fit. One of the lift's is "under renovation" for several months, leaving only one lift in operation and hence it took a long time to go up and down. Some of the staff at reception (not all - some were very helpful) had a poor attitude as did some of the housekeeping/room service operators (not the actual waiters who were very courteous). 

If there are any positives to take home the location is excellent and the bar staff in the Heist bar were very friendly and good company.

Definitely give this hotel a miss unless you get a very good deal - USD100-125 MAX per night!

title: Great location, average hotel that has the potential to be so much more
text:
Me and my boyfriend checked in here on 27th December 2010 until 7th Jan 2011, so were here over New Year. We did not book this until 18th Dec as a last minute deal.

When visiting Sri Lanka plan what you want to do before booking any accommodation. Whilst Sri Lanka is not a huge country the road systems are quite poor and there is a huge amount of traffic so getting anywhere takes time. If you stay on the south coast you wont get to see many sites on day trips but the beaches are nicest here. From Colombo you can just about visit places like Sigiriya in a day if you leave at 5am and get back at 7pm. The best way to see Sri Lanka is to stay a night or two at several hotels and move around the country. To see the sites you can hire a car (you will need an International driving licence before you go from your local post office for £5) or you can hire a car with a driver which is the option we took. It does not cost much more and you get to see everything without getting lost!

The hotel its self was OK, nothing special, but average. The door staff were always the most attentive, always pleased to talk to us and open the doors. No-one else seemed to care much.

By Sri Lankan standards the hotel room was fine, by Western standards it was average, nothing special. The room was cleaned daily but almost every day we would have to call reception for towels because they kept forgetting to replenish them. The bed linen has some cigarette burns from previous guests. The room has a side view of the sea but you cannot open the windows or take photos out of your window as the Presidents house is next to the hotel in a large compound. Every day there was a wedding, sometimes 2, and in the evenings, until the early hours, you could hear the discos!!

The pool area was clean and overlooks the sea, although there is a road between the pool and sea which you are not allowed on. As per other reviews we did get blue paint on us from the pool! The loungers were comfortable and on a couple of occassions had snacks by the pool which were fine, although the service was a little slow.

The breakfast buffet had a good selection but strangely sausages are cooked to order and are not cooked long enough unless you instruct the chef to do them well done.

We ate in the 'Tandoor' Restaurant about 4 times during our stay we loved it so much. The chefs are from India and you get genuine Indian food at a good price for a hotel. Everything is cooked fresh and you can see the kitchen. Service was good in here and we always managed to get a table.

The hotel bar had a happy hour each evening for 2 hours but be careful as not everything is buy one get free. Beer is, wine is not. Some cocktails are, some are not. The service can be slow but the free nuts and bits are lovely.

From the hotel you can go for a walk in the park or along the beach. At night as the sun comes down you often get lovely sun setsand you can grab some local food from the vendors on the beach and for very little money.

Overall a super location and we loved the Tandoor Restaurant but everything else was average.

The local people made us feel very welcome in their country and we even joined the locals for New Years Eve in a different local hotel. So many amazing sites, a wonderful Country

title: A good choice for New year's Eve
text:
We were given rooms by our travel agent at the Taj Samudra, but at the last minute we were shifted to the Continental, which apparently used to be the "Intercontinental". Well, it certainly has none of the quality that is associated with the Intercon, but it's not a bad option for the Colombo Seaface. Sure, the Hotel prides itself on being the oldest 5 star in SL and it shows, at times, but the sea facing rooms have a splendid view and the pool is gorgeous. 
We attended the NY Party there and we had a ball of a time - despite the corny theme of "Continental Air 2011" the local band was really good and we ended up having a super time. We heard from friends that the Taj party was absolute Bollywood so the rooms change was a blessing in disguise!
The Indian restaurant is pleasant enough, I wouldn't say it's totally authentic but makes for a nice dining option. The breakfast was alright. What really killed our experience was the painful check out process which took nearly forever.

title: Worst 5 Star
text: We stayed at the Ceylon Continental hotel for two nights in December 2010 and I have to say that it is the worst 5 star hotel I have encountered. We were apparently in a deluxe sea view room however the condition of the room suggested otherwise. Firstly, it was on the third floor of the hotel, secondly the pillowcases were filthy and there was hair in the bed sheets. There was barely even a view of the ocean. I spoke to the manager Chanaka and requested that the room be cleaned immediately off course in sri lanka nothing in  done immeditely. I also mentioned to him that the room is hardly of a deluxe standard. He promised to upgrade our rooms at 12pm the following day but this did not occur till 4.30pm the following day. The staff at the hotel were so busy that customer service was not a priority. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone in it's current condition. Perhaps wait till they complete their planned renos. This was by far the worst hotel we stayed in and even the location did not win me over. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: The glory of old days long gone ...
text:
I stayed in Ceylon continental  for 3 nights on a business trip in Sri Lanka in October. Well, the hotel definitely cannot be described as a 5-star hotel and I would need to close one eye to give it even 4-stars. 

I am not sure in what kind of 5-star hotels the previous traveller have stayed, but giving this hotel, although it has some good points too, 5-stars is a complete overstatement. 

You can see that the hotel has seen its good days, but these are long gone. The entire hotel from lobby to the rooms is in a desperate need of investment and refurbishment. The furniture in the rooms is very old, the size of TV that I haven't seen for years with really bad reception of channels. The bedlinen and towels must have been used for years too. The paint is coming off from the walls, especially in the bathroom and the entire feel gives you the impression that the hotel just woke up from a long sleep, perhaps 20 - 30 years. Neverthless, the rooms and bed are kept really clean and there is nothing I could critisize when it comes to cleanliness. 

The wi-fi is reasonable at just USD 10 for 24hour access. The main restaurant serving breakfast is OK with good breakfast and selection of local and international dishes for lunch and dinner. Reasonable prices, but the quality can definitely improve. The pool area is not very inviting and in 3 days I spent in the hotel I saw only 1 person in the pool. 

With regards location, its right on the beachfront, next to presidential palace and a few banks and government offices. 

To summarise, if you don't have high expectations you might choose this hotel. However, as far I am aware for the money you pay in Ceylon, you can easily stay in hotels of much higher quality like Taj and CInnamon Grand that are located in the same area. I guess, that will be my choice for the next stay in Colombo rather than returning to Ceylon..

title: decent hotel at a good location but renovation needed asap!
text:
We stayed at the Ceylon Continental Hotel for two nights in December 2010 towards the end of our Sri Lanka tour. We had high expectations from this '5 star' hotel but were a bit disappointed with the reality.

The staff is extremely helpful and friendly and want to make your stay as pleasant as possible. The location and views are great and one can hear the ocean at night quite clearly. The breakfast is really good as well. 

However, it is not quite a 5 star hotel. I say this because of the state of the rooms. While efforts are made to keep them clean, they are quite dated. The paint is chipping off the edges in some areas, the wooden furniture is losing its colour, the carpet in the corridor is fading and the room and bathroom doors are beginning to chip away as well. All these things do not make for an ideal stay but the rooms are still livable.

A room change was offerred but the other options were not too much better. The manager informed us that the complete renovation of the hotel is planned for Q1 2011. Until then, maybe they should stop advertising themselves as a 5 star hotel.

title: Dated but great location
text:
This is never a 5* hotel (3* at best). The first room we were shown was small, musty and damp-smelling. We ended up upgrading (for 200 USD per night) to the Ocean View suite, which was fantastic and as the name suggests had breathtaking views over the Indian Ocean. The suite comprised a bedroom, a kitchenette, a separate living/dining room and two bathrooms. 
The hotel is very popular with couples getting married and can be rather annoying at times when they block the entrance for photo opps. The food is quite ok. We would recommend the Indian restaurant on site (but not the atrocious live music they insist on playing). Children are not allowed in the bar at night which was very disappointing as it killed our evenings off early. We had never encountered this problem before anywhere else during our three week stay in Sri Lanka. 
Reception seems to have trust issues with its guests. Normally they are supposed to block an amount on your credit card for incidentals. However, as soon as we upgraded, they wanted payment for the room up front. 
On the whole, I would say this hotel is fine if you're staying in the Ocean View Suite - otherwise don't bother. We had dinner at the Lagoon Restaurant of the Cinammon Grand Hotel down the road, which was fantastic and that seems a much more upmarket hotel with bags of entertainment. If we ever went back, we'd stay there instead.

title: Superb Location but Average Experience
text:
The Ceylon Continental perhaps enjoys one of the best locations in downtown Colombo, right next to the vast expanse of the ocean and also on the perimeter of an extremely high security zone, given the President's Palance nearby. However, this hotel which severed its tie-up with the Intercontinental Group some time back, has the opportunity to be a far better hotel than what it can currently boast to be.

Given the awesome location, most of the rooms have stunning sea views and the rooms themselves are quite good, though a little cramped given that they are not very spacious. The service is good and the staff  friendly,  the hotel managers do make a genuine attempt to ensure you have a comfortable stay and for a business trip, the hotel is decent. The pool is nice and big, and the squash courts are a good option to unwind. But the gym is small, stuffy and very rundown, and not in line with the other fancier amenities. The other problem that the hotel suffers from is average food at the coffee shop (especially around lunch time) and limited choice of restaurants. The Indian restaurant is reasonable but the Italian place, with an ideal location next to the sea and with great views, was mysteriously empty and almost shut the two nights I stayed at the place - and no one really knew why ! So for a decent meal if you stay beyond one night, you neccesarily have to head out to town. The lobby is not as big and spacious as you would expect in other 5 star hotels in the city, and the look and feel a little rundown and cluttered. The other small though consequential issue (atleast for business travellers who travel a lot) is the inexplicable absence of any reward / miles program, that even the other local 5 star hotels in Colombo have. 

Not a bad place to stay for a 2-3 day business trip, but given the enviable location and the other myriad options in Colombo for work travel, some focus needs to be given to pull up the hotel to global standards.

title: Do not consider this hotel....PLEASE be warned!
text: We booked to stay at this hotel as part of a 16 day business trip and did not even spend 1 night here it was so bad. The hotel is dated and is NEVER  a 5 star property, it would struggle to be a 2 star!! The problems started with the airport pick up, it was a disaster, 3 passengers and 4 cases all crammed into a small estate car with a driver who spoke no English. On arrival we were shocked, the hotel is dated and the staff were in shockingly bad uniforms that were dirty and looked 5 years old. The key had the room number taped on to a piece of card. The lift was like something from the 1970's and the rooms were small and dirty. The bed had stains and the pillows were shocking, the bathroom was also dirty. We then sought the management assistance as we advised we would be moving to HILTON, they were shocked and offered us free nights for which we declined. We did move to Hilton which was much better and was at least a good 4 star standard. Please be warned if you are a seasoned traveller and used to 4 or 5 star standards DO NOT consider this hotel, you will regret it!!

title: Beware Booking this Hotel-They charge your card for full stay
text:
Beware Booking this Hotel-

They charge your card for full stay the day you book...the website says thay charge your card for one day...then take months to credit your account...because of this hotel I cancelled my trip to Sri Lanka...felt this was the example I would find there...they still have one day on my credit card and I am having problem getting it back.

title: Good hotel with appalling service
text:
This hotel is located in an excellent area of Colombo. Away from all busy and noisy part of the city this four star hotel is situated in a very pleasant place over looking the Indian Ocean. You will get some excellent views of the Indian Ocean from the room. I had a deluxe room which was clean but rather small. The breakfast was definitely not four star and the service was absolutely appalling. When I went to check in, I stood in front of the reception for at least good 7-8 minutes (I had only one person checking in before me). There were four staff at the front office and not one of them acknowledged me once or even looked at me. Finally, I had to approach them and even then they did not greet me or said sorry. I was absolutely disappointed as I have seen the friendliest and most smiley people on earth in this little paradise -Sri Lanka. On another occasion, I had to call the duty manager in to sort something out in my room. Having called the front desk four times and having waited more than an hour, I had to physically go and see the duty officer who was in the ground floor.
I do not know how this hotel has managed to employ who I think the most miserable and unfriendly staff in that entire island.

title: Nice Hotel but Disappointing service
text: The hotel was old but its nice.  Reception was very good and the staff in the restaurant.  But the room service, housekeeping & pool attendant was terrible.  Room service was very slow and when I ask the staff to bring me a honey on my tea he did'nt come back.  Housekeeping never went to clean our room and the pool attendant was so arrogant.

title: AbIsolutely Shocking - avoid at all costs
text:
I Stayed here with my wife for 2 nights and it cold well be one fo the worst hotels i've stayed in EVER. Do not under any circumstances get this hotel confused with an 'Intercontinental' hotel as it once was but is now most definitely not. 

Something that we were not told when booking this hotel is that the president of Sri Lanka lives a mere 30 metres away which means the area is heavily fortified with army personnel which is not a problem but means that there are numerous checkpoints all around and taxi's and tuk-tuks do not venture in unless they are carrying passengers, which invariably means you get ripped off taking the hotel ones. What it also means is that the area is not heavily invested in by the hotels and therefore Interconitnental took their name off this one and it is now just not 5-star.

The lobby is dated, the lift and rest of the hotel exclusively plays "I can't live, if livin is without you" ALL THE TIME. The rooms are small but this is to be expected in a capital city. The bathrooms was filthy and when i turned on the shower, brown water came out for about a minute before running clear. The basin taps leaked onto the floor, the flush leaked onto the floor and the tiny bathtub had rust in it. 

Location is good, views of the 'beach' are good and the bed is large and comfortable (we were in a king size room). We were in Colombo for a wedding which was taking place at the Cinnamon Grand down the road and upon meeting our friends in their room there, we wished we'd have stayed there. That hotel is 5-star. My wife had to get her hair done at the Taj and we also visitied the Hilton which meant we we had a good view of what a 5-star in Colombo should or could look like. The Ceylon continental would rank as a 3-star at best in comparison.

Breakfast was average, the room in which its served was kept at a such a cold temperature that there was water dripping off the aircon unit onto the floor. We duly complained about all this to the manager and he insisted he would upgrade us. The next day our bags were moved into another room and although 1 floor higher, all we could notice was that the bed was smaller. This apparently was the executive floor. We complained again and the best he could offer was a free meal (we mentioned we were here for a wedding so did not require a meal) or 25% off the additional room extras, i.e. the 6 local phonecalls we'd made.

Absolutely shocking service, highly recommend any other hotel in the city.

title: Beautiful Views of The Beach from Suite Rooms
text: The property is located in the high Security Area, hence moement is resticted. But the security are very courteous to visitors. Only issues is calling cabs, you have to use hotel cabs. The per room night rate is extremely cheap.

title: Wish it had been better
text:
We were first booked in another hotel. At our request, this was changed to the Ceylon Continental. This is a 5 star hotel mainly catering to business travellers. Being holiday travellers, we did not enjoy it as much. Security was too tight. Staff very intrusive. Even basic facility like a tea pot or an electric kettle was not provided. Dirnking glass came after a request was made.

The hotel did not live upto its 5 star reputation.

Krishnaswamy

title: Mixed experience at the Continental
text:
Stayed for 11 nights at this hotel.  My office is a stone's throw from the hotel (oh, don't throw anything.... there are armed guards everywhere).  I got a room facing the city ie facing the guards.  Didnt want the ocean view because the sound of waves crashing made me a bit edgy especially after the tsunami.  Besides the rooms get colder.

The room was nice.  They really should think of laying carpets in the room as the tiles make the room colder.  Ordered room service often.  Ordered sandwiches, and twice "roti special".  It has a filling of tandoori chicken marinated in curd, was really good stuff.  Went for the buffet twice, it was decent.  The breakfast buffet is limited on the meat front .... more of chicken, mutton and fish.  Beef was rarely seen.  The bacon was hidden away on the side of the hall.  This was probably due to the large number of tourists from the Gulf countries, Maldives and India.

Got a wifi card which had a validity of 4 hours and 7 days.  It couldn't be used after about two hours and 2 days.  I didn't bring it to the notice of the hotel management as I used to get back to the room tired and also because of the disappointing experience when I went to get the card in the beginning.

Staff behaviour was mixed, some were friendly, some indifferent.  But I must say that I appreciate their efforts considering the situation in their country. The gym was excellent, they've got two treadmills.  I might stay in this hotel again for the gym and also because it's close to the office.

title: Could do better
text:
I have stayed at this hotel every year for the last 3 years.  It's okay, but has been steadily going downhill.  The hotel is classed as five star, but I would class it at about 3 stars.  B&B rates vary according to the time of year, but averages out to about £35-£45 a day.  The rates are reasonable.  

The hotel was the former Intercon.  It's a bit dated.  The staff and reception are friendly, although there is a language barrier.  Some speak English very well, others not so well, but they'll give you the impression they understood everything you said.  Some of the rooms on the higher level have been refurbished, but those on the lower levels are in dire need of refurbishment.  Try and ask for an ocean view room on the rear of the hotel.  The rooms at the front don't offer a great view other than looking at the World Trade Centre and various police/army check points.  

During my stay I had to conistently ask for two towels a day.  They only left one in the room.  I often take two showers a day in a hot country and this is why.  They promised a newspaper everyday, but it didn't arrive.  I asked the front office manager is she could arrange one and she smiled and said it would be done.  But the paper still never arrived!  Room service is mediocre at best.  It is virtually non existent when there's a wedding.  All the room floors are tiled and the room staff tend to drag the beds across the room.  So, it is avisable to take a pair of earplugs with you if you want a decent sleep.  On check-in they gave me a room at the rear as requested, but the windows were so dirty I could not see out of them.  They gave me the room next door, which was a tad better.

The breakfast buffet is quite varied with a selection of hot and cold food, both Western and Eastern.  But I would not recommend the restaurant.  Service is poor and slow.  I ordered a typical Sri Lankan dish - a curry, but it came cold!!  I returned it and it came back 10 mins later, luke warm!  The only bar - the Heist - is off the lobby area and is very loud if they have a live group performing, which is usually on the weekends.  It is also expensive compared with other bars around Colombo centre.  They have recently banned smoking in this bar.  

Checkout is poor and sloppy.  It took them half an hour to check me out and I waited 15 mins for my bags to come down from the room, this was despite a taxi waiting on the forecourt.

When I checked my credit card statement a few weeks later, I noticed they'd charged what was the equivalent of 81 pence on my account.  I emailed them out of principle and questioned this charge.  They said they'd lost a room service chit for coffee I had ordered.  Hardly the actions of a "five star" hotel?  Most hotels five star or otherwise would have written off such a minor charge?

There's a pleasant sun terrace and swimming pool.  I would recommend the sun setting.  Worth a photo.

The hotel itself is right in the heart of Colombo next to the ocean.  The location is good for business travellers.  But it's in a high security area, so be warned that there'll be lots of armed police and military.  One night I counted 14 armed police outside the hotel.  So, if you don't like to be surrounded with people carrying loaded weapons, then this is not the place for you.  Even as a tourist I was stopped and questioned on several occasions at the many check points.  Is this a holiday?  Most guests were passing through.  I noticed a lot of Indian business people.  My overall impression is that it's cheap but certainly NOT five star both in terms of service or comfort.

title: Good value
text:
We contacted the hotel directly and got a fantastic last minute price, so couldn't really complain!

The communal areas (the lobbby, reception, bar, pool, restaurants) are all great and 5* standard. The rooms are OK - but do smell pretty damp. We have actually stayed here on 2 occassions now - and the second time we got a smoking room - and it actually smelt better as it masked the smell of the dampness!!

It is a very convenient and good value for money place to stop overnight. If you are planning to spend a few days in Colombo, I would probably spend a bit more and stay elsewhere!

title: lovely people ok hotel
text:
We recently stayed in this hotel. It has a good location and nice sea views but it is starting to fade. If you wanted a real 5 star hotel then I suggest the Hilton.

This was fine for cleanliness, food, service etc be prepared for taxi drivers who constantly want you to go on tour but I think that there is not many tourists so you are a target.

Do go to the House of Fashion and bring an empty suitcase to take back your purchases.

I did enjoy the hotel but I wouldn't rave about it!  fantastic all body massage though.

title: Cheap but not so Cheerful
text: It was certainly value for money in this case.  The 70's decor and stale smell in the lifts & hallways were not pleasant.  The cost of private cars must have gone up considerably since the last set of reviews were made because though many reviews within the last year state that a day will cost $25, its actually $40 - 45, even if you book directly with a driver.  In fact, a full day outside of Colombo with a private car & driver, which included stops at the Pinawella Elephant Orphanage, Kandy (not much to see there), and the Botantical Garden, was $100 for the full day, not including the tip, when booked with the Continental Hotel.  Unfortunately, the driver did not speak very good English either, so it was a rather challenging day.  The location is on the water, which is nice, but the overall experience was nothing special.

title: Good Value but......
text:
I had read that this superbly situated hotel (between the Indian Ocean and the historic Fort and Pettah areas)was renowned for its service, and indeed it could not be faulted on this criterion.  However, it is a hotel that needs attention if it is to retain its reputation.

The main problem is the size and quality of its single rooms.  They are claustrophobically small. The are also in desperate need of refurbishment. The furniture is chipped and scatched, whilst the bedcovers are worn and bobbled.  The bathroom had also seen better days.

The lobby and restataunts look as if they have been refurbished, and are of international standard.  

The buffet restaurant was superb with excellent Sri Lankan food (and the usual "international" offerings).
The lunch buffet is particularly good value at 1000 rupees (£5.75)inclusive of taxes. Indeed, all prices are quoted inclusive of the 26% taxes, and are thoroughly reasonable. The bar also has a "buy 1 get one free" offer in the early evening and from 10pm to 11pm. The early bar closing time was annoying if, like me, you fancied a night cap after a night on the town!

Overall, a good but not outstanding hotel that needs money spending on it sooner rather than later.  The service, however, could not be bettered and the staff were as attentive to the needs of an independent traveller as they were to business guests.
